You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

1: ===== documents/matters/1001-00002/Engagement & Administration/engagement-letter.docx =====
2: **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Counselors at Law* One Vanderbilt Avenue, 44th Floor New York, New York 10017
3: 
4: Telephone: (212) 814-6000 Facsimile: (212) 814-6001 www.calderwoodharkness.com
5: 
6: October 9, 2023
7: 
8: **VIA EMAIL AND HAND DELIVERY**
9: 
10: Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022
11: 
12: > Attention: Marcus Aldridge, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
13: >
14: > Priya Narayanan, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
15: 
16: Dear Mr. Aldridge and Ms. Narayanan:
17: 
18: We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.
19: 
20: **[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**
21: 
22: This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.
23: 
24: The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.
25: 
26: **[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**
27: 
28: The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.
29: 
30: **2.1 Entity Restructuring**
31: 
32: Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:
33: 
34: \(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.
35: 
36: \(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.
37: 
38: \(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.
39: 
40: \(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.
41: 
42: \(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.
43: 
44: \(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.
45: 
46: **2.2 Economics Realignment**
47: 
48: Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the reallocation and documentation of the economic arrangements among the principals of the Fund, including:
49: 
50: \(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.
51: 
52: \(b\) Drafting an amended and restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement reflecting the revised carried interest percentages applicable to each principal, including vesting schedules, forfeiture and clawback provisions, and mechanics for the allocation of carried interest among HoldCo members through the GP Intermediate and General Partner chain.
53: 
54: \(c\) Drafting a Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement at the HoldCo level, setting forth the allocation of management fee revenue among HoldCo members, including base compensation allocations, discretionary bonus pools, and distribution priorities.
55: 
56: \(d\) Revising the co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal group and to address any changes in co-investment rights and priorities resulting from the restructuring.
57: 
58: **2.3 Departing Principal Separation**
59: 
60: Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the negotiation and documentation of separation arrangements for two departing principals:
61: 
62: \(a\) **David Kellner** (Senior Partner), who is retiring from the Ardent Capital platform; and
63: 
64: \(b\) **Joanna Trask** (Partner), who is departing voluntarily.
65: 
66: In connection with each departing principal, the Firm will:
67: 
68: > \(i\) Draft comprehensive separation and release agreements, addressing, among other things, the departing principal\'s resignation from all positions with the ManCo, the General Partner, HoldCo (if applicable), and all affiliated entities; mutual releases of claims; confidentiality, non-disparagement, non-solicitation, and (as applicable) non-competition covenants; cooperation obligations; and any ongoing compensation or benefits arrangements.
69: >
70: > \(ii\) Draft carry retention and clawback side letters, specifying the portion of carried interest to be retained by each departing principal with respect to investments made during his or her tenure, the clawback obligations applicable thereto, and the mechanics for the calculation and payment of any retained carry distributions.
71: >
72: > \(iii\) As applicable, draft a senior advisor agreement in favor of Mr. Kellner, setting forth the terms of any ongoing advisory role, including the scope of services, compensation, expense reimbursement, and termination provisions.
73: >
74: > \(iv\) Coordinate, as necessary and appropriate, with Whitford & Chase LLP, counsel to the departing principals, led by Richard Beaulieu, Esq., in connection with the negotiation and finalization of all separation documentation.
75: 
76: **2.4 LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance**
77: 
78: Calderwood & Harkness will advise on all limited partner notification, consent, and compliance matters arising from the restructuring, including:
79: 
80: \(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.
81: 
82: \(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.
83: 
84: \(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.
85: 
86: \(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.
87: 
88: **2.5 Tax Structuring**
89: 
90: Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax analysis and structuring advice in connection with the restructuring, including:
91: 
92: \(a\) Federal income tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including the tax treatment of the contribution or transfer of interests in the General Partner and the ManCo to HoldCo.
93: 
94: \(b\) Delaware tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including any applicable Delaware franchise taxes, formation taxes, or annual reporting obligations.
95: 
96: \(c\) Federal income tax analysis of the reallocation of carried interest among the principals, including the application of Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code and any implications arising from the modification of existing partnership interests.
97: 
98: \(d\) Tax analysis of the economic arrangements with departing principals, including the characterization of carry retention payments and the tax treatment of any consideration paid in connection with the separation arrangements.
99: 
100: \(e\) Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) analysis of built-in gain allocations with respect to existing Fund investments, including the impact of the restructuring on the allocation of built-in gains and losses among the principals and the mechanics for tracking and allocating such amounts through the revised entity structure.
101: 
102: \(f\) All tax structuring advice under this engagement will be provided by Sylvia Hartwell, Specialist Partner (Tax), who will coordinate as necessary with the Client\'s independent accountants at Heathrow Whitman & Co.
103: 
104: **2.6 Limitations on Scope**
105: 
106: The scope of this engagement is limited to the matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:
107: 
108: \(a\) Routine fund operations, portfolio company transactions, and ongoing limited partner communications unrelated to the restructuring described herein. We understand that such matters will continue to be handled by Pemberton Hale LLP (Victoria Langford, Partner), which serves as the Fund\'s existing fund formation and operations counsel.
109: 
110: \(b\) Accounting, auditing, and valuation services, which we understand are provided by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (accountants and auditors) and Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation), respectively. Nothing in this engagement shall be construed as the provision of accounting, auditing, or valuation advice by Calderwood & Harkness.
111: 
112: \(c\) Representation of any departing principal, including David Kellner and Joanna Trask, in connection with the restructuring or any other matter. Each departing principal is separately represented by Whitford & Chase LLP.
113: 
114: \(d\) Representation of any limited partner of the Fund in connection with the restructuring or any other matter.
115: 
116: To the extent matters arise during the course of this engagement that fall outside the scope described herein but that may benefit from our involvement, we will discuss with the Client whether and on what terms such matters should be added to the scope of this engagement or addressed through a separate engagement.
117: 
118: **[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
119: 
120: The following attorneys will serve as the primary members of the engagement team:
121: 
122:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
123:   **Name**                **Role**                   **Responsibility**
124:   ----------------------- -------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
125:   Nicholas Stern          Responsible Partner        Overall supervision of the engagement, strategic advice, and senior-level involvement in key negotiations and decision points
126: 
127:   Graham Sutherland       Billing Partner            Billing, engagement administration, and fee-related communications
128: 
129:   Owen Fischer            Lead Associate             Day-to-day management of the engagement, including document drafting and negotiation, coordination with counterparty counsel (Whitford & Chase LLP) and other advisors (Pemberton Hale LLP, Heathrow Whitman & Co., Broadleaf Consulting Group)
130: 
131:   Stephen Adler           Working Associate          Document drafting, due diligence, preparation of regulatory filings, and research support
132: 
133:   Sylvia Hartwell         Specialist Partner (Tax)   Tax structuring advice, Section 704(b) and 704(c) analysis, and coordination with Heathrow Whitman & Co. on tax-related matters
134:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
135: 
136: From time to time, additional attorneys or paraprofessionals may be assigned to the engagement as the Firm deems necessary or appropriate to ensure efficient and timely completion of the workstreams described herein. The Client will be notified in advance of any such additions to the engagement team.
137: 
138: **[4. Fee Arrangement and Billing]{.underline}**
139: 
140: **4.1 Hourly Rates**
141: 
142: Fees for services rendered in connection with this engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:
143: 
144:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
145:   **Timekeeper Level**                **Hourly Rate**
146:   ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
147:   Partner                             \$1,650
148: 
149:   Specialist Partner                  \$1,750
150: 
151:   Senior Associate                    \$950
152: 
153:   Associate                           \$750
154:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
155: 
156: The foregoing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each year. In the event of any rate adjustment during the term of this engagement, the Firm will communicate such adjustment to the Client in advance. Adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.
157: 
158: **4.2 Estimated Fee Range**
159: 
160: Based on the anticipated scope and complexity of the engagement as described in Section 2 above, and taking into account the number of workstreams, the anticipated volume of document drafting and negotiation, and the extent of LP consent and regulatory compliance work expected to be required, we estimate that total professional fees for this engagement will fall within the range of **\$850,000 to \$1,100,000**.
161: 
162: This estimate is provided solely for budgeting purposes and does not constitute a cap, ceiling, or fixed fee. Actual fees may vary from this estimate based on a number of factors, including (without limitation) the ultimate scope and complexity of the work, the nature and duration of negotiations with Whitford & Chase LLP on behalf of the departing principals, the extent and complexity of LP consent solicitation and side-letter compliance matters, the number and complexity of tax structuring issues that arise, and any expansion of the scope of the engagement beyond the matters described herein. The Firm will endeavor to keep the Client informed on an ongoing basis of any circumstances that are likely to cause total fees to exceed the upper end of the estimated range, and will discuss with the Client any potential modifications to the scope or approach to the engagement that might mitigate such costs.
163: 
164: **4.3 Disbursements.** In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with the engagement. Disbursements may include, without limitation, filing fees (including Delaware Secretary of State filing fees for Certificates of Formation and other filings), messenger and courier charges, travel expenses (including transportation, lodging, and meals incurred in connection with travel reasonably necessary for the engagement), document production and reproduction costs, computerized legal research charges, and similar items. All disbursements will be itemized on the Firm\'s monthly invoices.
165: 
166: **4.4 Billing Procedures**
167: 
168: Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered monthly. All invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Invoices will be directed to:
169: 
170: > Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022
171: >
172: > Attention: Finance Department
173: 
174: Copies of all invoices will also be provided to Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan at the address set forth above, or at such other address or electronic mail address as the Client may designate in writing from time to time. The Client agrees to notify the Firm promptly if there is any question or dispute regarding any invoice, so that any such matter may be addressed in a timely manner.
175: 
176: **[5. Client Identity and Conflicts]{.underline}**
177: 
178: The Client for purposes of this engagement is Ardent Capital Management LLC. Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any individual principal of the Fund (including, without limitation, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, or any other continuing principal), any departing principal (including David Kellner and Joanna Trask), any limited partner of the Fund, or any other entity in the Ardent Capital structure (including, without limitation, the Fund, the General Partner, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, or any portfolio company) in their individual or separate capacities. Each such person and entity should consult with its own independent legal counsel with respect to any matter in which its interests may differ from those of the ManCo.
179: 
180: The Firm has conducted a conflict check in accordance with its standard procedures and, as of the date hereof, has identified no conflicts of interest that would preclude this engagement. In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of the engagement, the Firm will promptly notify the Client and take appropriate action, which may include seeking an informed written waiver of the conflict from the affected parties or, if a waiver cannot be obtained or is not appropriate under the circumstances, withdrawing from the representation in whole or in part as required by applicable rules of professional conduct.
181: 
182: **[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**
183: 
184: Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by or on behalf of the Client in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations and applicable rules of professional conduct. This obligation of confidentiality extends to all non-public information concerning the Fund, the General Partner, the ManCo, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, the principals (whether continuing or departing), the limited partners, the portfolio companies, and any other entities or persons about which information is provided to the Firm in connection with the engagement.
185: 
186: The Firm may disclose confidential information as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order, or with the prior written consent of the Client. In the event the Firm receives a subpoena, court order, or other compulsory process seeking the disclosure of confidential information relating to this engagement, the Firm will, to the extent permitted by law and practicable under the circumstances, provide prompt notice to the Client prior to making any such disclosure, so that the Client may seek protective measures or take other appropriate action.
187: 
188: **[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**
189: 
190: Calderwood & Harkness will retain engagement files, including correspondence, memoranda, agreements, and other documents generated or received in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, as in effect from time to time. Upon completion or termination of the engagement, the Firm will, at the Client\'s request and expense, return original documents to the Client or make arrangements for the transfer of files. Documents retained by the Firm may be destroyed in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy following the expiration of the applicable retention period, unless the Client requests in writing that such documents be returned or otherwise preserved.
191: 
192: **[8. Governing Law]{.underline}**
193: 
194: This Engagement Letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflict-of-laws principles thereof.
195: 
196: **[9. Termination]{.underline}**
197: 
198: Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. In the event of termination by either party, the Client will remain responsible for payment of all professional fees earned and disbursements incurred through the date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 4 above.
199: 
200: Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness will take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests, including cooperating in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client. The Firm will promptly deliver to the Client or its successor counsel all documents and materials necessary for the continued handling of the matter, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies of such documents in accordance with its document retention policy and applicable rules of professional conduct.
201: 
202: **[10. Acceptance and Counterparts]{.underline}**
203: 
204: We respectfully request that the Client confirm its acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement by having each of the undersigned representatives execute and return the enclosed copy of this Engagement Letter to Calderwood & Harkness at the address set forth above, or by transmitting an executed copy by electronic mail to Nicholas Stern at nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or Graham Sutherland at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com.
205: 
206: This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.
207: 
208: We look forward to working with you and the Ardent Capital team on this important matter. Please do not hesitate to contact either of us if you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement or if you would like to discuss any aspect of the representation in greater detail.
209: 
210: Very truly yours,

244: **ARDENT CAPITAL GP III LLC** 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, NY 10022
245: 
246: Registered Agent: Prestige Registered Agents LLC 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201 Dover, DE 19904
247:

259: 
260: **Re:** Ardent Capital Partners III LP --- Notification of Proposed Management Company Restructuring, Economics Realignment, and Departures of Senior Principals; Solicitation of LPAC Consent Pursuant to Section 9.4 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership
261: 
262: Dear Members of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee:
263: 
264: **[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**
265: 
266: Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"**General Partner**\"), as the sole general partner of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"**Fund**\" or \"**Fund III**\"), is writing to provide notification of, and to solicit the consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\" or the \"**Committee**\") to, a proposed restructuring of the management company and related realignment of economics among the Fund\'s principals (the \"**Restructuring**\"). This letter sets forth the material terms and circumstances of the Restructuring in detail, together with the background and rationale therefor, and identifies the specific consents being requested of the LPAC in connection therewith.
267: 
268: The consent of the LPAC is being solicited pursuant to **Section 9.4** of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund, dated as of April 15, 2019 (as amended, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"**LPA**\"), which requires LPAC consent for certain material structural changes to the General Partner, the management company, or the economic arrangements among the principals, including without limitation any change in the ownership or control of the General Partner, any material amendment to the organizational documents of the General Partner, and any material realignment of the carried interest or management fee economics of the Fund.
269: 
270: The General Partner respectfully requests that each LPAC member review this letter and the enclosed materials carefully and execute and return the enclosed Form of Written Consent (the \"**Consent**\") at or prior to the LPAC meeting scheduled for **February 14, 2024**, which will be held virtually via videoconference. Details regarding the videoconference will be provided under separate cover. LPAC members may deliver their consent either by execution and return of the enclosed Consent in advance of the meeting or by affirmative vote at the meeting itself.
271: 
272: In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner has engaged **Calderwood & Harkness LLP** (Nicholas Stern, responsible partner, and Owen Fischer, lead associate) as restructuring counsel to advise the General Partner on the structural, governance, and transactional aspects of the Restructuring. **Pemberton Hale LLP** (Victoria Langford, responsible partner) continues to serve as fund counsel for routine Fund operations and has provided guidance on LPA interpretation and side-letter compliance matters. The General Partner wishes to note that Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Pemberton Hale LLP represent the General Partner and the Fund, respectively, and do not represent any individual limited partner or the LPAC. LPAC members are encouraged to consult with their own legal and tax advisors as they deem appropriate.
273: 
274: **[2. Background on the Fund]{.underline}**
275: 
276: Ardent Capital Partners III LP is a Delaware limited partnership formed in 2019 for the purpose of making control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies, primarily in North America. The Fund targets companies with enterprise values between \$150 million and \$750 million, with a focus on sectors where the principals of Ardent Capital have deep operational expertise and established proprietary sourcing channels, including industrial technology, specialty distribution, environmental services, and facility management.
277: 
278: As of the date of this letter, the key parameters of the Fund are as follows:
279: 
280: **Total Commitments.** The Fund has aggregate capital commitments of **\$2.8 billion** from **47 limited partners**, including leading public pension systems, endowments and foundations, insurance companies, family offices, and other institutional investors.
281: 
282: **Capital Called and Invested.** As of the date of this letter, the Fund has called approximately **\$1.96 billion** in capital from its limited partners, representing approximately **70%** of total commitments. Of the capital called, approximately **\$1.88 billion** has been invested or is reserved for follow-on investments across the Fund\'s portfolio, with the remainder having been applied to management fees, organizational expenses, and other fund-level charges.
283: 
284: **Portfolio Overview.** The Fund currently holds **11 active portfolio companies** across the industrial and business-services sectors. Each portfolio company is actively managed by a dedicated deal team within Ardent Capital, and in each case Ardent Capital holds board representation and exercises significant operational influence.
285: 
286: **Fund Performance.** As of September 30, 2023, the most recent quarterly valuation date, the Fund\'s aggregate performance was as follows:
287: 
288: > • Gross multiple of invested capital (\"**MOIC**\"): **1.42x**
289: >
290: > • Net internal rate of return (\"**IRR**\"): **14.7%**
291: >
292: > • Total unrealized value: approximately **\$2.33 billion** (based on fair market valuations prepared by Broadleaf Consulting Group, the Fund\'s independent valuation advisor, and reviewed by Heathrow Whitman & Co., the Fund\'s auditor)
293: >
294: > • Total realized proceeds: approximately **\$445 million** (reflecting partial realizations and dividend recapitalizations from three portfolio companies)
295: 
296: **GP Commitment.** The General Partner and its principals have made an aggregate capital commitment to the Fund of **\$42 million**, representing **1.5%** of total Fund commitments, which is consistent with the minimum GP commitment described in the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum dated March 2019.
297: 
298: **Investment Period.** The investment period of the Fund commenced on June 30, 2019, and is scheduled to end on **June 30, 2025**. As of the date of this letter, the Fund has approximately \$840 million of uncalled capital commitments available for new investments during the remaining portion of the investment period.
299: 
300: **Fund Term.** The term of the Fund is scheduled to expire on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner in accordance with Section 12.1 of the LPA.
301: 
302: **Management Fee.** The Fund pays an annual management fee equal to **1.75%** of aggregate capital commitments during the investment period (approximately **\$49 million** per year at current commitment levels) and **1.50%** of invested capital (net of write-downs and write-offs) following the expiration of the investment period. The management fee is payable quarterly in advance to Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"**Management Company**\" or \"**ManCo**\"), the Fund\'s SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417).
303: 
304: **Carried Interest.** The General Partner is entitled to receive carried interest equal to **20%** of the Fund\'s net profits (calculated on a whole-Fund basis), subject to an **8% per annum preferred return** to the limited partners and a **100% catch-up** to the General Partner thereafter, in each case as more fully described in Section 6.2 of the LPA.
305: 
306: **Current Principals.** As of the date of this letter, the principals of the General Partner are:
307: 
308: > • **Marcus Aldridge** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
309: >
310: > • **Priya Narayanan** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
311: >
312: > • **David Kellner** --- Senior Partner
313: >
314: > • **Joanna Trask** --- Partner
315: >
316: > • **Robert Hsiao** --- Partner
317: 
318: **[3. Summary of Proposed Restructuring]{.underline}**
319: 
320: **3.1 Overview.** The Restructuring involves four principal workstreams, each of which is described in detail below:
321: 
322: > 1\. **Entity Restructuring** --- the formation of new holding entities and the reorganization of the ownership structure of the General Partner and the Management Company;
323: >
324: > 2\. **Economics Realignment** --- the reallocation of carried interest and Management Company profit-share economics among the remaining and next-generation principals;
325: >
326: > 3\. **Departing Principal Separation** --- the orderly departure and separation of two senior principals, David Kellner and Joanna Trask, and the negotiation and execution of their respective separation and release agreements; and
327: >
328: > 4\. **LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance** --- the solicitation of LPAC consent as required under the LPA and compliance with notification and consent provisions contained in individual side letters.
329: 
330: The principal rationale for the Restructuring is fourfold: (a) to implement a thoughtful succession plan that positions Ardent Capital for long-term stability and continuity across multiple fund cycles; (b) to enhance governance by establishing a consolidated holding company structure with clear lines of authority and accountability; (c) to integrate the next generation of talent --- specifically, Elena Marchetti and Samuel Okonkwo, each of whom has made significant contributions to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management --- into the economic and governance framework of Ardent Capital; and (d) to facilitate the orderly transition of responsibilities and economics following the planned departure of David Kellner (who is retiring after a distinguished career) and the voluntary departure of Joanna Trask. The General Partner believes that the Restructuring will strengthen Ardent Capital\'s institutional platform and is in the best interests of the Fund and its limited partners.
331: 
332: **3.2 Entity Restructuring**
333: 
334: The structural component of the Restructuring involves the formation of two new Delaware limited liability companies and the reorganization of the ownership structure of the General Partner and the Management Company. Specifically:
335: 
336: **Formation of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC.** A new Delaware limited liability company, **Ardent Capital Holdings LLC** (\"**HoldCo**\"), will be formed to serve as the parent holding company of both the Management Company and the General Partner (through an intermediate entity). HoldCo will be governed by an amended and restated limited liability company agreement that provides for the rights, obligations, and economic entitlements of its members.
337: 
338: **Formation of Ardent GP Intermediate LLC.** A new Delaware limited liability company, **Ardent GP Intermediate LLC** (\"**GP Intermediate**\"), will be formed to serve as an intermediate holding entity between HoldCo and the General Partner. GP Intermediate will be a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo.
339: 
340: **Post-Restructuring Organizational Structure.** Upon completion of the Restructuring, the organizational structure will be as follows:
341: 
342: > • HoldCo will be the **sole member** of both (i) the Management Company (Ardent Capital Management LLC, SEC-registered investment adviser, CRD #298417) and (ii) GP Intermediate.
343: >
344: > • GP Intermediate will be the **sole member** of the General Partner (Ardent Capital GP III LLC).
345: >
346: > • The General Partner will continue to serve as the sole general partner of the Fund.
347: 
348: **Current Structure Being Replaced.** Under the current organizational structure, the five individual principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) hold direct membership interests in both the General Partner and the Management Company. The direct-ownership model was adopted at the time of the Fund\'s formation for simplicity, but as Ardent Capital has grown and matured as an institution, the General Partner has determined that a consolidated holding company structure is more appropriate and consistent with industry best practices for institutional-quality private equity platforms. The holding company structure also facilitates the admission and withdrawal of individual principals without requiring amendments to the organizational documents of the General Partner or the Management Company, thereby reducing administrative burden and the need for LP consents in connection with future personnel changes (to the extent otherwise permitted under the LPA).
349: 
350: **HoldCo Membership.** Following the Restructuring, the members of HoldCo will be:
351: 
352: > • **Marcus Aldridge** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
353: >
354: > • **Priya Narayanan** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
355: >
356: > • **Robert Hsiao** --- Partner
357: >
358: > • **Elena Marchetti** --- Principal
359: >
360: > • **Samuel Okonkwo** --- Principal
361: 
362: The **Managing Members** of HoldCo will be Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, who will have the authority to manage the business and affairs of HoldCo (and, through HoldCo, the Management Company and the General Partner) in accordance with the terms of the HoldCo operating agreement.
363: 
364: **3.3 Principal Departures**
365: 
366: **David Kellner --- Retirement.** David Kellner, a Senior Partner of Ardent Capital and one of the founding members of the Fund III team, has informed the General Partner of his intention to retire from active investment management. Mr. Kellner, age 61, has had a distinguished 35-year career in private equity and has been instrumental in building Ardent Capital\'s industrial services franchise. His retirement will be effective **March 31, 2024**, following a transition period during which he will work with the remaining principals to ensure an orderly handover of his portfolio company board responsibilities and deal-team oversight functions. Following his retirement, Mr. Kellner will transition to a **Senior Advisor** role for a two-year advisory term (April 1, 2024 through March 31, 2026), during which he will be available for consultation on portfolio matters at an annual advisory fee of **\$350,000** per year.
367: 
368: The key economic terms of Mr. Kellner\'s departure are as follows:
369: 
370: > • **Current GP Interest:** Mr. Kellner currently holds a **15%** membership interest in the General Partner and is entitled to a **15%** share of the Fund\'s carried interest.
371: >
372: > • **Carried Interest Retention:** Mr. Kellner will retain **100%** of his vested carried interest in Fund III, which, based on the September 30, 2023 valuation, represents an accrued carried interest of approximately **\$13,140,000**. Such retained carried interest will be subject to a modified clawback obligation that will continue for a period of **three (3) years** following Mr. Kellner\'s retirement date (i.e., through March 31, 2027), at which time his clawback exposure will expire.
373: >
374: > • **Management Company Economics:** Mr. Kellner\'s share of ManCo profit distributions will cease effective as of his retirement date. He will receive no further profit-share or other economic distributions from the Management Company after March 31, 2024.
375: >
376: > • **Restrictive Covenants:** Mr. Kellner has agreed to a **non-competition** covenant for a period of **18 months** following his retirement date and **non-solicitation** covenants with respect to both employees and limited partners of Ardent Capital for a period of **24 months** each following his retirement date.
377: 
378: **Joanna Trask --- Voluntary Departure.** Joanna Trask, a Partner of Ardent Capital, has informed the General Partner of her decision to depart from Ardent Capital voluntarily to pursue a senior role at another investment firm. Ms. Trask, age 48, has been a valued member of the Ardent Capital team and has led several successful investments in the business-services sector during her tenure. Her departure will be effective **April 15, 2024**, following a transition period during which she will complete the handover of her responsibilities.
379: 
380: The key economic terms of Ms. Trask\'s departure are as follows:
381: 
382: > • **Current GP Interest:** Ms. Trask currently holds a **12%** membership interest in the General Partner and is entitled to a **12%** share of the Fund\'s carried interest.
383: >
384: > • **Carried Interest Retention:** Ms. Trask will retain **60%** of her vested carried interest in Fund III, representing approximately **\$6,307,200** based on the September 30, 2023 valuation. The remaining **40%** of her vested carried interest, representing approximately **\$4,204,800**, will be forfeited. In addition, Ms. Trask will forfeit **100%** of any unvested carried interest. Her retained carried interest will be subject to a clawback obligation for a period of **two (2) years** following her departure date (i.e., through April 15, 2026).
385: >
386: > • **Separation Payment:** Ms. Trask will receive a one-time lump-sum separation payment of **\$1,250,000**, payable within 30 days following her departure date, in consideration of her execution of a general release of claims and compliance with her ongoing restrictive covenants.
387: >
388: > • **Restrictive Covenants:** Ms. Trask has agreed to a **non-competition** covenant for a period of **12 months** following her departure date and **non-solicitation** covenants with respect to employees and limited partners of Ardent Capital for a period of **18 months** each following her departure date.
389: 
390: Both departures are subject to the terms of negotiated separation and release agreements (each, a \"**Separation Agreement**\") that are currently being finalized. Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask are each independently represented by **Whitford & Chase LLP** (Richard Beaulieu, partner) in connection with the negotiation of their respective Separation Agreements. Copies of the Separation Agreements (in substantially final form) will be made available to LPAC members upon request, subject to applicable confidentiality provisions.
391: 
392: **3.4 Economics Realignment**
393: 
394: Upon the effective dates of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, the aggregate **27%** carried interest share held by the departing principals (representing Mr. Kellner\'s 15% plus Ms. Trask\'s 12%) will be redistributed among the remaining and next-generation principals. The proposed post-Restructuring allocation of carried interest is set forth in the following table:
395: 
396:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
397:   **Principal**     **Pre-Restructuring Carry Share**   **Post-Restructuring Carry Share**   **Change**
398:   ----------------- ----------------------------------- ------------------------------------ -----------------
399:   Marcus Aldridge   35%                                 42%                                  +7%
400: 
401:   Priya Narayanan   30%                                 36%                                  +6%
402: 
403:   Robert Hsiao      8%                                  14%                                  +6%
404: 
405:   Elena Marchetti   0%                                  4%                                   +4%
406: 
407:   Samuel Okonkwo    0%                                  4%                                   +4%
408: 
409:   **Total**         **100%**                            **100%**                             **---**
410:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
411: 
412: The same percentage allocations reflected in the table above will apply to Management Company Profit Share distributions. For reference, Management Company Profit Share distributions (representing approximately 35% of annual management fee revenue retained by the Management Company after deduction of operating expenses) have averaged approximately **\$17,150,000 per year** over the life of the Fund to date. The economics realignment does not alter the overall quantum of management fees or carried interest payable by the Fund or its limited partners; rather, it reflects solely the internal allocation of such economics among the principals of the General Partner and the Management Company.
413: 
414: The following fundamental economic terms of the Fund remain **unchanged** by the Restructuring:
415: 
416: > • The carried interest rate remains at **20%** of net profits;
417: >
418: > • The preferred return remains at **8%** per annum;
419: >
420: > • The catch-up remains at **100%** to the General Partner;
421: >
422: > • The clawback structure remains unchanged, including **100% joint and several liability** of the General Partner and its principals, with a **30% individual escrow** of carried interest distributions (the \"**Escrow**\"); and
423: >
424: > • The mechanics of carried interest calculation (whole-Fund, European-style waterfall) remain unchanged.
425: 
426: With respect to **accrued carried interest**, as of September 30, 2023, the Fund\'s total accrued (but undistributed) carried interest was approximately **\$87,600,000**. The vested and retained portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s accrued carried interest will be carved out and preserved in accordance with the terms of their respective Separation Agreements, as described in Section 3.3 above. The redistribution set forth in the table above applies on a **go-forward basis** to carried interest attributable to future appreciation in the Fund\'s portfolio from and after the effective date of the Restructuring. The specific mechanics of the transition and allocation of accrued versus go-forward carry will be set forth in the amended carry allocation provisions of the GP\'s organizational documents and in Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.
427: 
428: **3.5 GP Commitment Reallocation**
429: 
430: The total GP commitment to the Fund is **\$42,000,000**. As a result of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, their combined unfunded GP commitment of **\$3,402,000** (consisting of \$1,890,000 attributable to Mr. Kellner and \$1,512,000 attributable to Ms. Trask) must be assumed by the remaining principals to ensure that the GP commitment is fully funded through the remainder of the investment period and the balance of the Fund\'s term. The funded portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s GP commitments will remain in the Fund and will be treated in accordance with their respective Separation Agreements and the LPA.
431: 
432: The unfunded portion of the departing principals\' GP commitment will be assumed by the remaining HoldCo members on a pro rata basis, consistent with their post-Restructuring percentage interests, as follows:
433: 
434:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
435:   **Principal**           **Post-Restructuring %**   **Assumed Unfunded GP Commitment**
436:   ----------------------- -------------------------- ------------------------------------
437:   Marcus Aldridge         42%                        \$1,428,840
438: 
439:   Priya Narayanan         36%                        \$1,224,720
440: 
441:   Robert Hsiao            14%                        \$476,280
442: 
443:   Elena Marchetti         4%                         \$136,080
444: 
445:   Samuel Okonkwo          4%                         \$136,080
446: 
447:   **Total**               **100%**                   **\$3,402,000**
448:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
449: 
450: Each remaining principal has confirmed his or her willingness and ability to fund the assumed unfunded GP commitment in accordance with the Fund\'s capital call schedule. The General Partner has received written commitments from each of the above-named individuals to this effect.
451: 
452: **[4. Key-Person Analysis]{.underline}**
453: 
454: Section 5.2 of the LPA designates **Marcus Aldridge** and **Priya Narayanan** as \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if: (a) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, or (b) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund and a replacement Key Person is not approved by the LPAC within 120 calendar days of such cessation.
455: 
456: The General Partner confirms that **neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person** under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Accordingly, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask **do not trigger a Key Person Event** under the LPA, and the investment period will continue without suspension or interruption.
457: 
458: Both Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan will continue to serve as Co-Founders and Managing Partners of Ardent Capital and will continue to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, consistent with their obligations under the LPA. Neither Mr. Aldridge nor Ms. Narayanan has any present intention to reduce his or her involvement with the Fund or to pursue other business activities that would be inconsistent with the Key Person requirements of Section 5.2.
