The undersigned, on behalf of Ardent Capital Management LLC, hereby acknowledge receipt of the foregoing Engagement Letter and agree to the terms and conditions set forth therein.

**Re:** Ardent Capital Partners III LP --- Notification of Proposed Management Company Restructuring, Economics Realignment, and Departures of Senior Principals; Solicitation of LPAC Consent Pursuant to Section 9.4 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership

Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"**General Partner**\"), as the sole general partner of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"**Fund**\" or \"**Fund III**\"), is writing to provide notification of, and to solicit the consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\" or the \"**Committee**\") to, a proposed restructuring of the management company and related realignment of economics among the Fund\'s principals (the \"**Restructuring**\"). This letter sets forth the material terms and circumstances of the Restructuring in detail, together with the background and rationale therefor, and identifies the specific consents being requested of the LPAC in connection therewith.

The consent of the LPAC is being solicited pursuant to **Section 9.4** of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund, dated as of April 15, 2019 (as amended, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"**LPA**\"), which requires LPAC consent for certain material structural changes to the General Partner, the management company, or the economic arrangements among the principals, including without limitation any change in the ownership or control of the General Partner, any material amendment to the organizational documents of the General Partner, and any material realignment of the carried interest or management fee economics of the Fund.

The General Partner respectfully requests that each LPAC member review this letter and the enclosed materials carefully and execute and return the enclosed Form of Written Consent (the \"**Consent**\") at or prior to the LPAC meeting scheduled for **February 14, 2024**, which will be held virtually via videoconference. Details regarding the videoconference will be provided under separate cover. LPAC members may deliver their consent either by execution and return of the enclosed Consent in advance of the meeting or by affirmative vote at the meeting itself.

In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner has engaged **Calderwood & Harkness LLP** (Nicholas Stern, responsible partner, and Owen Fischer, lead associate) as restructuring counsel to advise the General Partner on the structural, governance, and transactional aspects of the Restructuring. **Pemberton Hale LLP** (Victoria Langford, responsible partner) continues to serve as fund counsel for routine Fund operations and has provided guidance on LPA interpretation and side-letter compliance matters. The General Partner wishes to note that Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Pemberton Hale LLP represent the General Partner and the Fund, respectively, and do not represent any individual limited partner or the LPAC. LPAC members are encouraged to consult with their own legal and tax advisors as they deem appropriate.

**Fund Term.** The term of the Fund is scheduled to expire on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner in accordance with Section 12.1 of the LPA.

**Carried Interest.** The General Partner is entitled to receive carried interest equal to **20%** of the Fund\'s net profits (calculated on a whole-Fund basis), subject to an **8% per annum preferred return** to the limited partners and a **100% catch-up** to the General Partner thereafter, in each case as more fully described in Section 6.2 of the LPA.

> 4\. **LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance** --- the solicitation of LPAC consent as required under the LPA and compliance with notification and consent provisions contained in individual side letters.

**Current Structure Being Replaced.** Under the current organizational structure, the five individual principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) hold direct membership interests in both the General Partner and the Management Company. The direct-ownership model was adopted at the time of the Fund\'s formation for simplicity, but as Ardent Capital has grown and matured as an institution, the General Partner has determined that a consolidated holding company structure is more appropriate and consistent with industry best practices for institutional-quality private equity platforms. The holding company structure also facilitates the admission and withdrawal of individual principals without requiring amendments to the organizational documents of the General Partner or the Management Company, thereby reducing administrative burden and the need for LP consents in connection with future personnel changes (to the extent otherwise permitted under the LPA).

Both departures are subject to the terms of negotiated separation and release agreements (each, a \"**Separation Agreement**\") that are currently being finalized. Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask are each independently represented by **Whitford & Chase LLP** (Richard Beaulieu, partner) in connection with the negotiation of their respective Separation Agreements. Copies of the Separation Agreements (in substantially final form) will be made available to LPAC members upon request, subject to applicable confidentiality provisions.

With respect to **accrued carried interest**, as of September 30, 2023, the Fund\'s total accrued (but undistributed) carried interest was approximately **\$87,600,000**. The vested and retained portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s accrued carried interest will be carved out and preserved in accordance with the terms of their respective Separation Agreements, as described in Section 3.3 above. The redistribution set forth in the table above applies on a **go-forward basis** to carried interest attributable to future appreciation in the Fund\'s portfolio from and after the effective date of the Restructuring. The specific mechanics of the transition and allocation of accrued versus go-forward carry will be set forth in the amended carry allocation provisions of the GP\'s organizational documents and in Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.

The total GP commitment to the Fund is **\$42,000,000**. As a result of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, their combined unfunded GP commitment of **\$3,402,000** (consisting of \$1,890,000 attributable to Mr. Kellner and \$1,512,000 attributable to Ms. Trask) must be assumed by the remaining principals to ensure that the GP commitment is fully funded through the remainder of the investment period and the balance of the Fund\'s term. The funded portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s GP commitments will remain in the Fund and will be treated in accordance with their respective Separation Agreements and the LPA.

Section 5.2 of the LPA designates **Marcus Aldridge** and **Priya Narayanan** as \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if: (a) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, or (b) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund and a replacement Key Person is not approved by the LPAC within 120 calendar days of such cessation.

The General Partner confirms that **neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person** under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Accordingly, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask **do not trigger a Key Person Event** under the LPA, and the investment period will continue without suspension or interruption.

Both Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan will continue to serve as Co-Founders and Managing Partners of Ardent Capital and will continue to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, consistent with their obligations under the LPA. Neither Mr. Aldridge nor Ms. Narayanan has any present intention to reduce his or her involvement with the Fund or to pursue other business activities that would be inconsistent with the Key Person requirements of Section 5.2.

Additionally, the General Partner has identified that **3 of the 6** side letters containing expanded key-person provisions grant the applicable limited partner a right to request a **90-day suspension** of the investment period pending LPAC review in the event of a Contributing Person\'s departure. The General Partner does not believe that such a suspension is warranted in light of (i) the continued full-time involvement of both designated Key Persons (Aldridge and Narayanan), (ii) the orderly nature of Mr. Kellner\'s planned retirement and transition to a Senior Advisor role, (iii) the depth and continuity of the remaining investment team, and (iv) the ongoing strong performance of the Fund\'s portfolio. The General Partner intends to engage directly and proactively with each of the applicable limited partners to discuss these matters and to address any questions or concerns.

**Co-Investment Priority Rights.** Nine (9) of the 14 side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner co-investment priority rights or preferential co-investment allocation rights. The General Partner intends to update its internal co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal allocations and team responsibilities resulting from the Restructuring. The fundamental co-investment allocation framework --- which is based on commitment size, co-investment track record, and ability to respond to allocation opportunities within the required timeframe --- will remain substantively unchanged. LPAC members with co-investment priority rights will continue to receive advance notice of co-investment opportunities in accordance with their respective side letters.

**Material Change Notification and Consent Provisions.** Four (4) side letters --- those with **Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System**, **Pinnacle Insurance Group**, **Crestwood Endowment Partners**, and **Haverford Capital Partners** --- contain provisions requiring prior written notice and, in certain cases, affirmative consent to any \"material change in the management structure\" of the General Partner, the Management Company, or the Fund\'s investment team. This letter and the LPAC consent process described herein serve as the required notification to the three LPAC members (Ridgeline, Pinnacle, and Crestwood) that hold such provisions. Separate notice will be provided to Haverford Capital Partners in accordance with the specific requirements of its side letter.

A detailed **Side-Letter Compliance and Key-Person Analysis Memorandum** is currently being finalized by Pemberton Hale LLP and Calderwood & Harkness LLP. This memorandum, which will include a provision-by-provision analysis of each side letter and a comprehensive key-person analysis, will be made available to LPAC members upon request. LPAC members who wish to receive a copy of the memorandum should contact Nicholas Stern at Calderwood & Harkness LLP or Victoria Langford at Pemberton Hale LLP.

The General Partner wishes to assure the LPAC that the Restructuring has been designed to ensure continuity and stability in the Fund\'s operations and to minimize any disruption to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management. Specifically, the General Partner confirms that the Restructuring will have **no impact** on the following:

> • **Investment Strategy:** The Fund\'s investment strategy --- control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies --- will remain unchanged. The Fund will continue to pursue its stated investment objectives in accordance with the investment guidelines and restrictions set forth in the LPA and the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum.

> • **Carried Interest Terms:** The carried interest rate of **20%** of net profits, the **8%** preferred return, the **100%** catch-up, and all other terms of the carried interest waterfall and clawback provisions of the LPA will remain unchanged.
> • **Fund Term:** The term of the Fund will remain as set forth in the LPA, expiring on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner.

The SEC **Form ADV** for Ardent Capital Management LLC (CRD #298417) will be amended to reflect the updated ownership structure and personnel changes resulting from the Restructuring. The General Partner anticipates filing the amended Form ADV within **30 days** of the closing of the Restructuring and will provide a copy of the amended Form ADV to any limited partner that requests it.
Pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, the General Partner respectfully requests that each member of the LPAC consent to each of the following actions in connection with the Restructuring:

> 4\. **Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.** The execution and delivery of **Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership** of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, reflecting the structural changes to the General Partner and the Management Company described herein, including updated definitions, representations, and organizational chart references, as necessary to conform the LPA to the post-Restructuring organizational structure.

Consent may be delivered by execution and return of the enclosed **Form of Written Consent** to the attention of Marcus Aldridge or Nicholas Stern at the addresses set forth in Section 11 below, or by affirmative vote at the LPAC meeting scheduled for February 14, 2024. Under Section 9.4(c) of the LPA, the affirmative consent of a majority of the members of the LPAC (i.e., at least three of the four current LPAC members) is required for each of the actions described above.

**[A. LPA Key-Person Provisions (Section 5.2)]{.underline}**
Section 5.2 of the LPA designates Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan as the \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if:

> \(b\) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund and is not replaced by a substitute approved by the LPAC within one hundred twenty (120) days of such cessation.

Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the Fund\'s investment period is automatically suspended, and the General Partner may not make new investments (other than follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies and investments for which binding commitments have been entered into prior to the Key Person Event) until either (i) the LPAC approves a substitute Key Person, or (ii) the LPAC waives the Key Person Event by affirmative vote.
Neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Their departures do not, individually or in combination, constitute a Key Person Event under the LPA.

Notwithstanding the absence of a Key Person Event under the LPA, certain side letters contain \"expanded key person\" provisions that extend the scope of the key person framework beyond the two designated Key Persons.

> \(b\) **Investment Period Suspension Right:** Three (3) of the six side letters containing expanded key person provisions grant the affected limited partner the right to request a suspension of the Fund\'s investment period for a period of ninety (90) days, during which time the LPAC will review the circumstances of the departure and determine whether any further action is warranted.

The General Partner intends to engage proactively with the affected limited partners to discuss these matters and to respond to any questions or concerns.

Line 342: The principal Solara contacts for the intake were Priya Narasimhan, General Counsel, and Stefan Dalmqvist, Head of Tax. Additional financial data, including aggregate fair market valuations, adjusted tax basis information, and liability schedules, were confirmed during the May 26 call by Douglas Wexford, Chief Financial Officer. Ms. Narasimhan and Mr. Dalmqvist indicated that their internal team has been developing the reorganization concept since early 2025 and has already obtained preliminary approval from the LP Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\"), as discussed in further detail below.
Line 344: The purpose of this memorandum is to establish the factual foundation for the preparation and submission of a private letter ruling (\"PLR\") request to the Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR request will seek confirmation of the intended tax-free treatment of a multi-step cross-border reorganization of Solara\'s fund platform and the continued partnership classification of the resulting entities for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The reorganization involves the domestication and consolidation of four offshore fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, with corresponding distributions to limited partners and migration of investor classes into appropriate feeder vehicles.
Line 380: **A. Overview.** Solara currently operates through six parallel fund vehicles spanning three jurisdictions --- Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. These six vehicles are divided across two vintage-year fund families: Fund IV (vintage 2021) and Fund V (vintage 2023). Each fund family consists of three parallel vehicles: a Delaware limited partnership for U.S. taxable investors, a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership for non-U.S. and U.S. tax-exempt investors, and a Luxembourg special limited partnership (société en commandite spéciale, or \"SCSp\") for certain European and Asian non-U.S. investors requiring access to Luxembourg\'s extensive bilateral tax treaty network or preferring a regulated European domicile for internal governance reasons.
Line 382: As of the date of intake, the total number of portfolio companies held across all six vehicles is twenty-three (23), of which eleven (11) are held by Fund IV vehicles and twelve (12) are held by Fund V vehicles. Certain portfolio companies are held jointly across the Delaware and offshore vehicles within the same vintage, reflecting parallel investment structures in which each vehicle invests pro rata alongside the others in each portfolio investment.
Line 386: **B. Fund IV Family**
Line 388: The Fund IV family reached its final close on June 15, 2021, and comprises the following three vehicles:
Line 390: **1. Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP.**
Line 406: Fund IV LP is the domestic anchor vehicle for the Fund IV family. It is the largest single vehicle by committed capital within Fund IV and serves as the lead investment vehicle, with the offshore parallel vehicles generally co-investing in identical portfolio company transactions on a pro rata basis according to each vehicle\'s available capital. The limited partnership agreement of Fund IV LP was most recently amended and restated as of June 15, 2021 (the \"Fund IV LPA\"), and governs investor rights, fee arrangements, carried interest allocations, and other material terms. A copy of the Fund IV LPA has been requested from the Client as part of our initial data request.
Line 408: **2. Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP.**
Line 424: Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP serves two primary investor populations: (a) non-U.S. investors, such as sovereign wealth funds and non-U.S. insurance companies, that invest through the Cayman vehicle for tax efficiency and to minimize direct U.S. filing obligations; and (b) U.S. tax-exempt investors, such as public pension funds and university endowments, that invest through the Cayman vehicle to achieve UBTI blocker benefits via offshore corporate subsidiary holding structures interposed between the fund and debt-financed portfolio investments. This vehicle co-invests alongside Fund IV LP in each Fund IV portfolio company on a pro rata basis.
Line 426: **3. Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp.**
Line 442: Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp was established to accommodate non-U.S. investors --- principally European institutional investors and certain Asian investors --- that preferred investment through a Luxembourg-domiciled vehicle for treaty access, regulatory familiarity, or internal governance mandate reasons. The Luxembourg SCSp is a tax-transparent entity under Luxembourg domestic law and is treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. This vehicle co-invests alongside Fund IV LP and Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP in the Fund IV portfolio.
Line 444: **C. Fund V Family**
Line 446: The Fund V family reached its final close on September 30, 2023, and comprises the following three vehicles:
Line 448: **1. Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP.**
Line 464: Fund V LP is the largest single fund vehicle in the Solara platform and represents the domestic anchor vehicle for the Fund V family. Given its relatively recent vintage, a substantial portion of committed capital remains undeployed. The limited partnership agreement of Fund V LP was executed as of September 30, 2023 (the \"Fund V LPA\"). Stefan Dalmqvist noted during the May 26 call that Fund V LP has the most recent and investor-favorable governance provisions among the Solara fund documents, and that the Consolidated Master Fund LP\'s partnership agreement will likely be modeled on the Fund V LPA.
Line 466: **2. Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP.**
Line 482: Fund V-A (Cayman) LP serves the same investor populations as Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, as described above. The vehicle is registered with CIMA and administered by Clarendon Fund Services Ltd.
Line 484: **3. Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp.**
Line 500: Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp serves the same investor profile as Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp. Stefan Dalmqvist noted during the intake call that the Luxembourg vehicles have attracted modestly higher capital commitments in Fund V relative to Fund IV, reflecting increased allocations from European institutional investors, but that the OECD Pillar Two developments discussed in Section V below have diminished the forward-looking rationale for maintaining separate Luxembourg-domiciled vehicles.
Line 506: **U.S. Taxable Investors.** U.S. taxable investors --- including high-net-worth individuals, family offices, and U.S. taxable institutional investors --- invest through the Delaware main funds (Fund IV LP and Fund V LP). These investors receive annual Schedule K-1s from the Delaware partnerships and report their allocable shares of fund income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit on their individual or entity-level U.S. federal income tax returns. A representative investor in this category is Argyle Family Office Holdings LLC, a Delaware-organized family office with its principal office in Greenwich, Connecticut. Argyle\'s principal is Elliot Argyle. Argyle committed \$95 million to Fund IV LP and \$130 million to Fund V LP.
Line 508: **U.S. Tax-Exempt Investors.** U.S. tax-exempt investors --- including public pension funds, state retirement systems, university endowments, and certain foundations --- invest through the Cayman parallel vehicles (Fund IV-A Cayman and Fund V-A Cayman) to achieve UBTI blocker benefits. Specifically, these investors typically access the fund through one or more offshore corporate subsidiary holding structures interposed between the Cayman fund vehicle and the underlying debt-financed portfolio investments, thereby blocking unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") that would otherwise be generated by the use of fund-level or portfolio-level leverage. Representative investors in this category include:
Line 510: > • **Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System** --- a public pension fund established under the laws of the State of Pinnacle. Pinnacle committed \$275 million to Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP and \$340 million to Fund V-A (Cayman) LP. The Chief Investment Officer is Margaret Faulkner.
Line 512: > • **Grandview University Endowment** --- a university endowment established by Grandview University, a private university organized under the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Grandview committed \$120 million to Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP and \$185 million to Fund V-A (Cayman) LP. The Director of Investments is Harold Kingsley.
Line 516: > • **Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund** --- a sovereign wealth fund established by the Kingdom of Nordhaven. Nordhaven committed \$380 million to Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP and \$500 million to Fund V-A (Cayman) LP. The Head of Alternative Investments is Anders Bjørkman. Nordhaven has engaged independent tax counsel, Bramhall & Quelwick LLP (San Francisco, CA), to evaluate U.S. withholding tax and treaty implications of the proposed reorganization.
Line 518: > • **Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group** --- a Singapore-domiciled insurance group. Kestrel committed €200 million to Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp and €275 million to Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp. The Senior Portfolio Manager responsible for the Solara allocation is Christine Leung. Kestrel selected the Luxembourg vehicles for regulatory and treaty-related reasons specific to Singapore-Luxembourg bilateral arrangements.
Line 527:   NovaBright Data Systems Inc.    Delaware corporation; data center operator                                              \$890M           \$520M                   \$370M              Fund IV-A Cayman (60%), Fund IV LP (40%)
Line 529:   Crestline Cloud Solutions LLC   Delaware LLC (disregarded entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes); SaaS platform   €340M (\$367M)   €195M (\$211M)           €145M (\$156M)      Fund IV-B Lux (100%)
Line 531:   Veridian Edge Computing Corp.   Delaware corporation; edge computing infrastructure                                     \$1.12B          \$780M                   \$340M              Fund V-A Cayman (55%), Fund V LP (45%)
Line 533:   Thorngate Fiber Networks LP     Delaware LP; fiber-optic network operator                                               \$670M           \$490M                   \$180M              Fund IV-A Cayman (100%)
Line 535:   Helix SaaS Holdings Ltd.        Cayman Islands exempted company; SaaS holding company                                   \$445M           \$310M                   \$135M              Fund V-A Cayman (100%)
Line 538: These five portfolio company interests are representative of the broader portfolio and have been selected for inclusion in this memorandum because they present the most significant built-in gain positions and illustrate the range of entity types, jurisdictions, and holding structures across the platform. matches.line: This Letter sets forth the terms and conditions upon which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the matter described herein. By countersigning this Letter in the space provided below, the Client agrees to be bound by the terms and conditions set forth herein. This engagement shall be effective as of the date of the countersignature below. No attorney-client relationship will be deemed to have been established with respect to the matter described herein until this Letter has been signed by an authorized representative of the Client and returned to the Firm.

Solara is undertaking a cross-border reorganization of its fund platform (the \"Reorganization\"), involving the domestication and merger of several Cayman Islands and Luxembourg fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization is designed to simplify the Client\'s fund architecture, reduce administrative and operational costs, enhance investor reporting, and achieve certain tax efficiencies in connection with the ongoing management and eventual disposition of portfolio company interests.
The Reorganization involves the following existing fund vehicles (collectively, the \"Legacy Fund Vehicles\"):

> \(i\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$4.2 billion in committed capital (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of the date hereof;

> \(ii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$1.85 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors;

> \(iii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.15 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.24 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for certain European institutional investors;

> \(iv\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$5.6 billion in committed capital (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of the date hereof;

> \(v\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$2.45 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; and

> \(vi\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.38 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.49 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for certain European institutional investors.
The Reorganization contemplates the formation of the following new entities (collectively, the \"New Fund Vehicles\"):
> \(i\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership to serve as the master fund in a restructured master-feeder architecture;

The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction that includes, among other things, asset contributions by the four offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the dissolution of the legacy offshore vehicles following such contributions, and the migration of existing limited partners into the appropriate new feeder structure. The target effective date for the completion of the Reorganization is December 1, 2025. The precise sequencing and mechanics of the multi-step transaction will be developed and refined in the course of the engagement, in consultation with the Client and its other advisors.

> \(a\) **Tax Analysis Memoranda.** Preparation of comprehensive tax analysis memoranda addressing the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization under, among other provisions, Internal Revenue Code (\"IRC\") §§ 721(a), 721(b), 723, 731(a), 731(c), 704(c), 752, 367(a), 367(b), 1446, and 897, and Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3. The tax analysis memoranda will address the characterization of each step of the multi-step Reorganization, including the contribution of assets by the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the treatment of assumed or shifted liabilities, the application of the anti-mixing bowl rules, and the withholding tax implications for non-U.S. limited partners.

The purpose of this memorandum is to establish the factual foundation for the preparation and submission of a private letter ruling (\"PLR\") request to the Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR request will seek confirmation of the intended tax-free treatment of a multi-step cross-border reorganization of Solara\'s fund platform and the continued partnership classification of the resulting entities for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The reorganization involves the domestication and consolidation of four offshore fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, with corresponding distributions to limited partners and migration of investor classes into appropriate feeder vehicles.

**A. Overview.** Solara currently operates through six parallel fund vehicles spanning three jurisdictions --- Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. These six vehicles are divided across two vintage-year fund families: Fund IV (vintage 2021) and Fund V (vintage 2023). Each fund family consists of three parallel vehicles: a Delaware limited partnership for U.S. taxable investors, a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership for non-U.S. and U.S. tax-exempt investors, and a Luxembourg special limited partnership (société en commandite spéciale, or \"SCSp\") for certain European and Asian non-U.S. investors requiring access to Luxembourg\'s extensive bilateral tax treaty network or preferring a regulated European domicile for internal governance reasons.

As of the date of intake, the total number of portfolio companies held across all six vehicles is twenty-three (23), of which eleven (11) are held by Fund IV vehicles and twelve (12) are held by Fund V vehicles. Certain portfolio companies are held jointly across the Delaware and offshore vehicles within the same vintage, reflecting parallel investment structures in which each vehicle invests pro rata alongside the others in each portfolio investment.
**B. Fund IV Family**
The Fund IV family reached its final close on June 15, 2021, and comprises the following three vehicles:
**1. Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP.**

Fund IV LP is the domestic anchor vehicle for the Fund IV family. The limited partnership agreement of Fund IV LP was most recently amended and restated as of June 15, 2021 (the \"Fund IV LPA\"), and governs investor rights, fee arrangements, carried interest allocations, and other material terms. Consolidation of the four offshore vehicles into a single Delaware-domiciled Consolidated Master Fund LP, with two Cayman feeder vehicles (one for non-U.S. investors and one for U.S. tax-exempt investors), would substantially reduce these recurring costs. Solara estimates annual savings of approximately \$2.1 million in external fees and a meaningful reduction in internal staff time. The current multi-jurisdictional fund structure creates duplicative reporting obligations under the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\") and the OECD\'s Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\"). Each offshore vehicle is separately registered as a reporting financial institution under FATCA and CRS in its jurisdiction of organization, resulting in separate FATCA reporting to the IRS (via the Cayman Islands and Luxembourg intergovernmental agreements) and separate CRS reporting to the relevant local tax authorities for exchange with other participating jurisdictions. The consolidation of the four offshore vehicles into a Delaware master fund with two Cayman feeders would simplify these compliance obligations by reducing the number of reporting entities from four to two (the two remaining Cayman feeders), while the consolidated master fund would report directly to the IRS as a domestic partnership.

Overview.** The proposed reorganization consists of five integrated steps, planned for execution in the fourth quarter of 2025, with a target effective date of December 1, 2025 for the final step. The reorganization is designed to domesticate and merge the four offshore fund vehicles --- Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp, Fund V-A (Cayman) LP, and Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp --- into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, the Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP. Following the reorganization, the platform will consist of three Delaware partnerships (the existing Fund IV LP, the existing Fund V LP, and the new Consolidated Master Fund LP), together with two Cayman Islands feeder partnerships (one for non-U.S. investors and one for U.S. tax-exempt investors) that will invest through the Consolidated Master Fund LP. The five steps of the proposed reorganization are described in detail below.

The engagement team notes at the outset that the multi-step nature of the transaction raises potential step transaction doctrine issues, which will need to be addressed in the PLR request. The steps are structured to occur over a period of approximately ten weeks (from the target date for Step 2 on October 1, 2025, through the target effective date for Step 5 on December 1, 2025) and are designed to be independently meaningful and separately motivated, but the IRS may seek to collapse the steps for analytical purposes. The PLR request will need to address the step transaction doctrine proactively, as discussed further in Section VIII below.

**C. Step 2 --- Contribution of Fund IV-A Cayman Assets (Target: October 1, 2025)**

In Step 2, Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP will contribute all of its portfolio assets --- consisting of interests in portfolio companies, cash, and other fund-level assets --- to the newly formed Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund. The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of Step 2 is as a tax-free contribution under IRC § 721(a), which provides that no gain or loss shall be recognized to a partnership or to any of its partners in the case of a contribution of property to the partnership in exchange for an interest in the partnership. No gain or loss would be recognized by Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP as the contributing partner or by the Consolidated Master Fund LP as the receiving partnership.

> • **Carryover Basis.** Under IRC § 723, the Consolidated Master Fund LP will take a carryover basis in the contributed assets equal to the adjusted tax basis of such assets in the hands of Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP immediately prior to the contribution. This preserves the \$690 million built-in gain for future recognition upon a taxable disposition of the contributed assets.

> • **Holding Period Tacking.** Under IRC § 1223(2), the Consolidated Master Fund LP\'s holding period in the contributed assets will include the period during which Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP held such assets, provided the assets were capital assets or property described in IRC § 1231 in the hands of the contributing partner. This tacking is critical for preserving long-term capital gain treatment on future dispositions.

44: **3.1 Overview of the Transaction**
45: 
46: Solara is undertaking a cross-border reorganization of its fund platform (the \"Reorganization\"), involving the domestication and merger of several Cayman Islands and Luxembourg fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization is designed to simplify the Client\'s fund architecture, reduce administrative and operational costs, enhance investor reporting, and achieve certain tax efficiencies in connection with the ongoing management and eventual disposition of portfolio company interests.
47: 
48: The Reorganization involves the following existing fund vehicles (collectively, the \"Legacy Fund Vehicles\"):
49: 
50: > \(i\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$4.2 billion in committed capital (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of the date hereof;
51: >
52: > \(ii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$1.85 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors;
53: >
54: > \(iii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.15 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.24 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for certain European institutional investors;
55: >
56: > \(iv\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$5.6 billion in committed capital (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of the date hereof;
57: >
58: > \(v\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$2.45 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; and
59: >
60: > \(vi\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.38 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.49 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for certain European institutional investors.
61: 
62: The Reorganization contemplates the formation of the following new entities (collectively, the \"New Fund Vehicles\"):
63: 
64: > \(i\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership to serve as the master fund in a restructured master-feeder architecture;
65: >
66: > \(ii\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund;
67: >
68: > \(iii\) **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors; and
69: >
70: > \(iv\) **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors.
71: 
72: The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction that includes, among other things, asset contributions by the four offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the dissolution of the legacy offshore vehicles following such contributions, and the migration of existing limited partners into the appropriate new feeder structure. The target effective date for the completion of the Reorganization is December 1, 2025. The precise sequencing and mechanics of the multi-step transaction will be developed and refined in the course of the engagement, in consultation with the Client and its other advisors.

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Attorneys at Law*
600 Lexington Avenue, 38th Floor New York, New York 10022
Telephone: (212) 554-8000 Facsimile: (212) 554-8001 www.calderwoodharkness.com

Priya Narasimhan, Esq. General Counsel Solara Digital Infrastructure LP 1200 Market Street, Suite 3400 Wilmington, Delaware 19801
> **Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Private Letter Ruling Request in Connection with Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP**
> **Engagement Number: 20250527-SDILP-PLR**
Dear Ms. Narasimhan:
**[1. Purpose and Acceptance]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (\"Solara\" or \"SDILP\"), a Delaware limited partnership, and its general partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (\"Solara GP\"), a Delaware limited liability company (collectively, the \"Client\"), to provide the legal services described in this engagement letter (this \"Letter\"). We appreciate the confidence that Solara and Solara GP have placed in our Firm, and we look forward to working with your team on this significant and complex matter.

This Letter sets forth the terms and conditions upon which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the matter described herein. By countersigning this Letter in the space provided below, the Client agrees to be bound by the terms and conditions set forth herein. This engagement shall be effective as of the date of the countersignature below. No attorney-client relationship will be deemed to have been established with respect to the matter described herein until this Letter has been signed by an authorized representative of the Client and returned to the Firm.
**[2. Description of the Client]{.underline}**

The client for this engagement is Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN: 82-4917366) and Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN: 82-4917365). For the avoidance of doubt, the \"Client\" as used throughout this Letter refers collectively to SDILP and Solara GP, except where the context clearly requires otherwise.

Solara is a Delaware-based private equity sponsor with approximately \$14.7 billion in assets under management as of March 31, 2025, operating across digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS verticals. Solara sponsors private equity funds through a series of parallel fund structures established across Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and Luxembourg to accommodate U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S. investor pools. The fund platform reflects a multi-jurisdictional architecture that is common among institutional-scale private equity sponsors and is central to the reorganization that is the subject of this engagement.
The principal contact persons at Solara for purposes of this engagement are as follows:
> • **Priya Narasimhan**, General Counsel --- primary legal contact and authorized decision-maker for engagement-related matters;
> • **Stefan Dalmqvist**, Head of Tax --- primary contact for substantive tax matters, financial data, and coordination with the Client\'s independent auditors and valuation advisors.

The Managing Partner and Founder of Solara is **Viktor Raines**. Mr. Raines will serve as the authorized officer of Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC for purposes of executing any penalties of perjury declarations and other representations required in connection with Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") submissions, as described more fully in Section 8 below.
All communications from the Firm regarding this engagement should be directed to Ms. Narasimhan and Mr. Dalmqvist, unless otherwise instructed in writing by the Client.
**[3. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**
**3.1 Overview of the Transaction**

Solara is undertaking a cross-border reorganization of its fund platform (the \"Reorganization\"), involving the domestication and merger of several Cayman Islands and Luxembourg fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization is designed to simplify the Client\'s fund architecture, reduce administrative and operational costs, enhance investor reporting, and achieve certain tax efficiencies in connection with the ongoing management and eventual disposition of portfolio company interests.
The Reorganization involves the following existing fund vehicles (collectively, the \"Legacy Fund Vehicles\"):

> \(i\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$4.2 billion in committed capital (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of the date hereof;

> \(ii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$1.85 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors;

> \(iii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.15 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.24 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for certain European institutional investors;

> \(iv\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$5.6 billion in committed capital (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of the date hereof;

> \(v\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$2.45 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; and

> \(vi\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.38 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.49 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for certain European institutional investors.
The Reorganization contemplates the formation of the following new entities (collectively, the \"New Fund Vehicles\"):
> \(i\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership to serve as the master fund in a restructured master-feeder architecture;
> \(ii\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund;
> \(iii\) **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors; and
> \(iv\) **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors.

The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction that includes, among other things, asset contributions by the four offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the dissolution of the legacy offshore vehicles following such contributions, and the migration of existing limited partners into the appropriate new feeder structure. The target effective date for the completion of the Reorganization is December 1, 2025. The precise sequencing and mechanics of the multi-step transaction will be developed and refined in the course of the engagement, in consultation with the Client and its other advisors.
**3.2 Scope of Legal Services**
Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement is limited to the following specific legal services in connection with the Reorganization:

> \(a\) **Tax Analysis Memoranda.** Preparation of comprehensive tax analysis memoranda addressing the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization under, among other provisions, Internal Revenue Code (\"IRC\") §§ 721(a), 721(b), 723, 731(a), 731(c), 704(c), 752, 367(a), 367(b), 1446, and 897, and Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3. The tax analysis memoranda will address the characterization of each step of the multi-step Reorganization, including the contribution of assets by the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the treatment of assumed or shifted liabilities, the application of the anti-mixing bowl rules, and the withholding tax implications for non-U.S. limited partners.

> \(b\) **Private Letter Ruling Request.** Drafting, revising, and finalizing a private letter ruling request (the \"PLR Request\") to be submitted to the Internal Revenue Service\'s Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR Request will seek rulings on the specific tax consequences of the Reorganization that are identified in the course of the engagement as requiring advance IRS guidance for purposes of transaction certainty.

> \(c\) **Ancillary IRS Procedural Documents.** Preparation and filing of all ancillary IRS procedural documents required in connection with the PLR Request, including IRS Forms 2848 (Powers of Attorney and Declarations of Representative), penalties of perjury declarations, user fee transmittals, and pre-submission and supplemental correspondence with the IRS.

> \(d\) **Pre-Submission Conference.** Coordination and participation in a pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL (requested for July 22, 2025) and any follow-up communications arising therefrom. The pre-submission conference is intended to confirm the jurisdictional assignment of the PLR Request, identify any threshold legal issues, and facilitate an efficient review process following formal submission.

> \(e\) **Submission of PLR Request.** Submission of the PLR Request to the IRS at the following address: Internal Revenue Service, Attn: CC:INTL, 1111 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20224, together with all required enclosures, exhibits, and transmittal documents.

> \(f\) **Post-Submission Monitoring.** Post-submission monitoring of the status of the PLR Request, preparation of responses to IRS information requests and additional questions, and supplemental submissions as necessary through issuance of the private letter ruling or closure of the matter by the IRS. This includes attendance at any conferences or telephone calls requested by the IRS examining branch.

> \(g\) **Coordination with Other Advisors.** Coordination with the Client\'s other advisors as described in Section 3.3 below, to the extent necessary for the preparation and prosecution of the PLR Request and associated tax analysis memoranda.

> \(h\) **Supporting Documentation.** Preparation of supporting documentation in connection with the Reorganization, including review of and comment on IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) filings for the New Fund Vehicles and any related check-the-box elections.
**3.3 Coordination with Other Advisors**

Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with, but does not assume responsibility for the work of, the following advisors that have been retained by Solara or its affiliates in connection with the Reorganization or related matters. Each of the following advisors has been engaged separately by the Client, and the Firm\'s coordination with such advisors is limited to the exchange of information and consultation necessary for Calderwood & Harkness to perform the services described in Section 3.2:

> \(i\) **Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP** (400 Renaissance Center, Suite 2500, Detroit, MI 48243; Helen Okamoto, Partner) --- independent accounting firm providing annual audits, tax compliance services, and supporting financial data for the PLR Request, including fund-level financial statements, capital account schedules, and partner allocation computations.

> \(ii\) **Redstone Advisory Group LLC** (750 Seventh Avenue, 21st Floor, New York, NY 10019; Marco DeLuca, Managing Director) --- valuation and transfer pricing advisory firm preparing fair market value appraisals of portfolio company interests and other assets to be contributed in connection with the Reorganization. Redstone\'s valuation reports will be included as exhibits to the PLR Request.

> \(iii\) **Meridian Offshore Legal** (Caledonia House, 69 Dr. Roy\'s Drive, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1103; Fiona McAllister, Partner) --- Cayman Islands counsel advising on the formation of the New Fund Vehicles organized in the Cayman Islands, the dissolution of the Legacy Fund Vehicles organized in the Cayman Islands, and related regulatory matters involving the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (\"CIMA\").

> \(iv\) **Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l.** (22, boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg; Marc Gérard, Managing Partner) --- Luxembourg counsel advising on the dissolution of the Luxembourg SCSp vehicles and notification requirements to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (\"CSSF\").

> \(v\) **Clarendon Fund Services Ltd.** (Windward 3, Regatta Office Park, West Bay Road, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1108; Rachel Okonkwo, Client Relationship Director) --- fund administrator for the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles, providing net asset value computations, investor registries, and other administrative data relevant to the Reorganization.

Calderwood & Harkness will rely upon the work product of the foregoing advisors to the extent necessary for the preparation of the PLR Request and associated tax analysis memoranda. However, the Firm assumes no responsibility for the accuracy, completeness, or timeliness of work product prepared by any such advisor, and the Firm\'s reliance on such work product will be subject to the Firm\'s independent professional judgment.
**3.4 Matters Excluded from Scope**
For the avoidance of doubt, this engagement does not include the following:

> \(a\) Legal advice on the laws of the Cayman Islands or Luxembourg, including corporate, partnership, regulatory, or tax law of those jurisdictions. Such matters are addressed by Meridian Offshore Legal and Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l., respectively, as described in Section 3.3 above.

> \(b\) Ongoing tax compliance for any fund vehicle, including preparation of federal, state, or local tax returns, Schedules K-1, FATCA reporting (including IRS Forms W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, and W-8IMY), or Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\") reporting.

> \(c\) Post-ruling implementation of the Reorganization, including without limitation the filing of formation documents, execution of contribution agreements, amendment and restatement of limited partnership agreements, or preparation or filing of dissolution documents, except to the extent specifically set forth in Section 3.2 above.

> \(d\) Legal advice to, or representation of, any individual limited partner of any Legacy Fund Vehicle or New Fund Vehicle, the LP Advisory Committee of any fund (including the Fund IV LP Advisory Committee and the Fund V LP Advisory Committee), or any counterparty to any transaction involving Solara or its affiliates.
> \(e\) State and local tax advice, including analysis of state income, franchise, or other tax consequences of the Reorganization in any U.S. state or local jurisdiction.

> \(f\) Investment advice or securities law analysis, including advice under the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, or any state \"blue sky\" laws.

If the Client wishes to expand the scope of this engagement to include any of the foregoing matters or any other matters not described in Section 3.2, the parties will enter into a separate engagement letter or written amendment to this Letter.
**[4. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
The following attorneys of Calderwood & Harkness will serve as the engagement team for this matter:

**Leonard Cross** --- Responsible Partner, Tax. Mr. Cross has twenty-eight (28) years of experience in international tax, partnership tax, and fund formation matters, with particular focus on cross-border restructurings, private letter ruling requests, and IRS controversy matters. Mr. Cross is located in Calderwood & Harkness\'s Washington, D.C. office at 1900 K Street NW, Suite 1100, Washington, DC 20006. He will serve as the primary point of contact for substantive tax matters and all communications with the IRS, including representation at the pre-submission conference and any subsequent IRS conferences or calls.

**Sylvia Hartwell** --- Billing Partner, Tax. Ms. Hartwell has twenty-four (24) years of experience in cross-border restructurings and investment fund taxation, with deep expertise in multi-jurisdictional fund platform redesigns. Ms. Hartwell is located in Calderwood & Harkness\'s New York office at 600 Lexington Avenue, 38th Floor, New York, NY 10022. She will be responsible for billing, budget management, engagement administration, and overall client relationship management. Ms. Hartwell will also contribute to the substantive tax analysis as needed.

**Robert Jansen** --- Lead Associate, Tax. Mr. Jansen has six (6) years of experience in tax law, with a focus on partnership taxation, entity classification, and IRS procedural matters. Mr. Jansen is located in the Firm\'s Washington, D.C. office. He will serve as the lead drafter of the PLR Request and tax analysis memoranda.

**Garrett Simmons** --- Working Associate, Tax. Mr. Simmons has three (3) years of experience in tax law, with a focus on international tax research and financial modeling. Mr. Simmons is located in the Firm\'s New York office. He will provide research support, drafting assistance, and financial modeling in connection with the tax analysis memoranda and the PLR Request.

Calderwood & Harkness may, from time to time, engage additional attorneys or professional staff to assist with the matter as the needs of the engagement require. The Client will be notified of any material change to the staffing plan described above, including the assignment of any additional partner-level attorney to the engagement team. The Firm will endeavor to staff the engagement in a manner that balances efficiency, continuity, and the appropriate level of expertise for each task.
**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**
**5.1 Hourly Rates**

Legal services rendered in connection with this engagement will be billed at a blended hourly rate of **\$1,175.00 per hour** for all engagement team members. The blended rate applies uniformly to all timekeepers assigned to the engagement, including partners, associates, counsel, and any other attorneys who may be assigned to the matter from time to time.

Calderwood & Harkness\'s standard billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each calendar year. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the blended rate of \$1,175.00 per hour will be maintained for the duration of this engagement and will not be adjusted unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Calderwood & Harkness and the Client.
**5.2 Estimated Fees**

Based on the scope of services described in Section 3, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total legal fees for this engagement will be in the range of **\$1,800,000 to \$2,400,000**. This estimate reflects the Firm\'s current understanding of the complexity of the Reorganization, the anticipated number of issues to be addressed in the PLR Request, and the expected level of IRS engagement.

This estimate is provided for budgeting purposes only and does not constitute a cap, maximum, fixed fee, or guaranteed price. The matter will be billed on a time-and-materials basis, and the Client will be responsible for actual fees incurred regardless of whether they fall within the estimated range.

Actual fees may be higher or lower than the estimate depending on a number of factors, including but not limited to: the complexity of tax issues encountered during the course of the engagement; the number of drafts of the PLR Request and tax analysis memoranda required; the extent and nature of IRS engagement, including the number and duration of conferences, information requests, and supplemental submissions; any expansion of the scope of services; and the availability and completeness of financial and transactional data provided by the Client and its other advisors.

Calderwood & Harkness will provide quarterly budget-to-actual comparisons to the Client and will promptly advise the Client if fees are projected to exceed the estimated range. The Firm will work collaboratively with the Client to manage costs and to ensure that the Client is informed of budgetary developments on a timely basis.
**5.3 Fee Cap / Budget**

There is no fee cap on this engagement. As noted in Section 5.2, the matter is billed on a time-and-materials basis. Quarterly budget updates will be provided to the Client, and the Firm will promptly notify the Client of any material developments that are expected to result in fees significantly exceeding the estimated range.
**5.4 Disbursements and Expenses**

In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of all reasonable disbursements and out-of-pocket expenses incurred by Calderwood & Harkness in connection with the engagement. Estimated total disbursements for the engagement are approximately **\$85,000**, and are expected to include the following categories:

> \(i\) **IRS User Fee:** \$38,000, payable in connection with the submission of the PLR Request. This amount reflects the current schedule of user fees applicable to ruling requests involving multiple entities with combined assets exceeding \$50 million, as set forth in the IRS\'s annual revenue procedure governing letter ruling requests (Rev. Proc. 2025-1 equivalent).

> \(ii\) **Travel Expenses:** Reasonable travel expenses for the pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL in Washington, D.C. (scheduled for July 22, 2025) and any subsequent IRS meetings or conferences, including airfare, hotel, ground transportation, and meals.
> \(iii\) **Courier and Filing Costs:** Sundial Data Systems, courier, and filing costs associated with the submission of the PLR Request and related documents to the IRS.

> \(iv\) **Document Reproduction:** Costs of copying, printing, and binding the PLR Request and exhibits for submission to the IRS, including production of multiple copies as required by IRS procedures.
> \(v\) **Electronic Research:** Costs of electronic legal research (e.g., Westmark Data Systems, Tidewater Technologies, Sundial Solutions) incurred in connection with the engagement.

All disbursements will be billed at cost without markup. The Firm will exercise reasonable judgment in incurring disbursements and will seek the Client\'s prior approval for any individual disbursement exceeding \$5,000 (other than the IRS user fee).
**5.5 Billing Cycle and Payment Terms**
Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered on a **monthly** basis, typically within fifteen (15) business days following the close of each calendar month.

Payment is due within **thirty (30) days** of the date of each invoice (net 30 days). Late payments may be subject to interest at the rate of 1.0% per month (12.0% per annum) on the outstanding balance, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

Each invoice will include detailed time entries reflecting the date of service, the name of the timekeeper, the number of hours billed, a narrative description of the services rendered, and the applicable hourly rate. Disbursements will be itemized separately.
All inquiries regarding invoices, billing, or payment should be directed to **Sylvia Hartwell** at (212) 554-8142 or shartwell@calderwoodharkness.com.
**[6. Matter Identification]{.underline}**

This engagement has been assigned Calderwood & Harkness matter number **20250527-SDILP-PLR**. All time entries, correspondence, work product, and billing will be recorded under this matter number. The Client should reference this matter number in all communications with the Firm regarding this engagement.

The matter has been opened in the Firm\'s records as of May 27, 2025. The administrative opening date reflects the Firm\'s internal processing timeline and does not alter the effective date of this engagement, which is as set forth in Section 1 above.
**[7. Key Milestones and Timeline]{.underline}**
The following target milestones have been identified for the engagement in consultation with the Client:
**Target Date**                     **Milestone**
June 16, 2025                       Completion of initial comprehensive tax analysis memorandum
July 1, 2025                        Circulation of draft PLR Request (Version 1.0) to Client for review
July 15, 2025                       LPAC review of final PLR Request draft
July 22, 2025                       Pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL Branch 1
August 15, 2025                     Submission of PLR Request to IRS

The foregoing dates are targets and are subject to change based on the progress of the engagement, the availability of financial and transactional data from the Client and its advisors, and the IRS\'s scheduling of the pre-submission conference. Calderwood & Harkness will use commercially reasonable efforts to adhere to the timeline set forth above and will promptly advise the Client of any anticipated delays.

Post-submission milestones relating to entity formation, execution of transactional documents, and the implementation of the Reorganization steps are outside the primary scope of this engagement but will be coordinated with the Client as necessary. For reference, the Client has identified the following additional target dates: formation of the New Fund Vehicles (September 15, 2025) and the Step 5 effective date for completion of the Reorganization (December 1, 2025).
**[8. IRS Procedural Matters]{.underline}**

The PLR Request will be submitted to the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\") of the Internal Revenue Service, with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The jurisdictional assignment reflects the cross-border nature of the Reorganization and the involvement of both international tax provisions (including IRC §§ 367(a), 367(b), 1446, and 897) and partnership tax provisions (including IRC §§ 721, 723, 731, 704(c), and 752).

A pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL has been requested for **July 22, 2025**. The purpose of the pre-submission conference is to discuss the proposed PLR Request in general terms, confirm the jurisdictional assignment, identify any threshold legal or procedural issues, and facilitate an efficient post-submission review process. Mr. Cross and Mr. Jansen will attend the pre-submission conference on behalf of the Client.

IRS Forms 2848 (Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative) will be filed with the IRS designating **Leonard Cross** and **Sylvia Hartwell** as authorized representatives for Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN: 82-4917366), Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN: 82-4917365), and all related fund entities involved in the Reorganization. A penalties of perjury statement, as required by Rev. **[I. Purpose of Memorandum]{.underline}**

This memorandum summarizes the facts received from Solara Digital Infrastructure LP\'s (\"Solara\" or the \"Client\") in-house legal and tax teams during two initial intake calls conducted on May 22, 2025, and May 26, 2025, in advance of the formal matter opening on May 27, 2025. The May 22 call was approximately ninety minutes in duration and focused primarily on the existing fund structure and business rationale for the proposed reorganization. The May 26 call was approximately two hours in duration and covered the proposed multi-step transaction, the representative portfolio company holdings, the aggregate financial parameters of the reorganization, and outstanding data needs. Both calls were conducted by videoconference, with Robert Jansen and Garrett Simmons participating from Calderwood & Harkness\'s Washington, D.C. and New York offices, respectively.

The principal Solara contacts for the intake were Priya Narasimhan, General Counsel, and Stefan Dalmqvist, Head of Tax. Additional financial data, including aggregate fair market valuations, adjusted tax basis information, and liability schedules, were confirmed during the May 26 call by Douglas Wexford, Chief Financial Officer. Ms. Narasimhan and Mr. Dalmqvist indicated that their internal team has been developing the reorganization concept since early 2025 and has already obtained preliminary approval from the LP Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\"), as discussed in further detail below.

The purpose of this memorandum is to establish the factual foundation for the preparation and submission of a private letter ruling (\"PLR\") request to the Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR request will seek confirmation of the intended tax-free treatment of a multi-step cross-border reorganization of Solara\'s fund platform and the continued partnership classification of the resulting entities for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The reorganization involves the domestication and consolidation of four offshore fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, with corresponding distributions to limited partners and migration of investor classes into appropriate feeder vehicles.

This memorandum is organized as follows: Section II provides an overview of the Client; Section III details the existing fund structure; Section IV describes representative portfolio company holdings; Section V sets forth the business rationale for the reorganization; Section VI outlines the proposed multi-step transaction; Section VII presents the aggregate financials; Section VIII identifies preliminary tax issues and the rulings to be requested; Section IX catalogs key third parties and advisors; Section X presents the target timeline; Section XI addresses IRS submission logistics; Section XII summarizes engagement information; Section XIII details outstanding data requests and next steps; and Section XIV addresses confidentiality and privilege matters.
