Line 12: > **Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- GP Advisory Regarding Key-Person Event, Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd.**
Line 20: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), a Delaware limited liability company (EIN: 82-4917653), in its capacity as the General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership registered with the Cayman Islands Registrar of Exempted Limited Partnerships under Registration No. ELP-87234. This engagement letter sets forth the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to DCM and the Fund in connection with the Key Person Event (as defined below) and related governance matters described herein.
Line 22: The Fund is governed by its Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated March 15, 2017 (as amended from time to time, the \"A&R LPA\"), which is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. The A&R LPA provides for certain key-person protections in favor of the Fund\'s limited partners, as more fully described in Section 3 below.
Line 24: This engagement is precipitated by the medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (holding a ninety percent (90%) membership interest) of DCM. Mr. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and has been incapacitated since that date. Mr. Whitmore is the sole individual designated as a \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. As a result of Mr. Whitmore\'s continued incapacitation for a period exceeding seven consecutive calendar days from the date of the medical event, a Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA is deemed to have been triggered as of June 10, 2024 (the \"Key Person Event\"). The occurrence of the Key Person Event gives rise to a number of contractual obligations, rights, and remedies under the A&R LPA that require prompt legal attention and careful navigation by DCM in its capacity as General Partner of the Fund.
Line 26: This engagement letter confirms the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to the Clients (as defined below) in connection with the Key Person Event, including, without limitation, analysis of the A&R LPA\'s key-person provisions, preparation of required limited partner notifications, development of a successor governance framework, drafting of LPA amendments, and coordination of the limited partner consent solicitation process.
Line 36: It is important that the scope of this representation be clearly understood. C&H represents DCM and DARF as described herein and does not represent any individual limited partner of the Fund, the Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund (the \"IAC\"), or any individual member or officer of DCM in his or her personal capacity. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, C&H does not represent Mr. Whitmore individually, nor does C&H represent any member of the IAC in his, her, or its individual or fiduciary capacity. Each such person and entity is encouraged to seek independent legal counsel to the extent such person or entity deems it necessary or appropriate.
Line 42: C&H\'s representation of the Clients will encompass the following workstreams in connection with the Key Person Event triggered under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA. Each workstream is described in further detail below.
Line 46: C&H will undertake a comprehensive analysis of the mechanics and consequences of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, including the following:
Line 48: > \(a\) **Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of \"Key Person.\"** C&H will confirm the scope of the \"Key Person\" designation under the A&R LPA, which identifies Marcus J. Whitmore as the sole designated Key Person. C&H will analyze the definition for purposes of establishing the factual predicate for the Key Person Event and for advising on the requirements for designating any Successor Key Person(s) (as described in Section 3.3 below).
Line 50: > \(b\) **Section 8.04(b) --- Trigger Conditions.** C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore\'s incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. Based on the information provided to C&H, Mr. Whitmore has been continuously incapacitated since June 3, 2024, and the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold was met as of June 10, 2024. C&H will prepare a memorandum confirming the legal basis for this determination.
Line 52: > \(c\) **Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of the Key Person Event.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the full range of consequences triggered by the occurrence of the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, which include the following:
Line 54: > \(i\) *Immediate Suspension of the Investment Period.* The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA) is automatically suspended upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event. During such suspension, the General Partner may not make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund, except as provided in clause (ii) below.
Line 56: > \(ii\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* Notwithstanding the suspension of the Investment Period, the General Partner retains limited authority to make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not to exceed one percent (1%) of the Fund\'s assets under management as of the date of the Key Person Event. Based on the Fund\'s most recently reported AUM of approximately \$2.87 billion, the follow-on investment cap is \$28.7 million.
Line 62: > \(v\) *LP Consent Threshold.* Approval of any proposed Successor Key Person(s) requires the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate capital commitments of all limited partners of the Fund, excluding for this purpose any co-investment by the General Partner. C&H will advise on the calculation of this threshold based on the most current LP commitment schedule maintained by the Fund\'s administrator.
Line 64: > \(d\) **Consequences of Failure to Cure.** C&H will further analyze the consequences under Section 8.04(d) of the A&R LPA if no cure is achieved within the Cure Period, including the limited partners\' right to elect, by the same 66⅔% consent threshold described above, either (x) to extend the Cure Period for one or more additional periods or (y) to direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund\'s portfolio. C&H will advise the Clients on the mechanics, timing, and fiduciary considerations associated with each of these alternatives.
Line 66: > \(e\) **Delaware Law Fiduciary Duty Analysis.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the fiduciary duties owed by DCM, as General Partner, to the limited partners of the Fund during the Key Person Event and throughout the consent solicitation process, as a matter of Delaware law. This analysis will address, among other things, the duty of care and the contractual modification of fiduciary duties under the A&R LPA, including the exculpation and indemnification provisions set forth in Article XII thereof.
Line 70: C&H will draft the formal written notice to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund disclosing the occurrence of the Key Person Event in compliance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA (the \"Key Person Notice\"). The Key Person Notice will describe the factual basis for the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences thereof, the commencement and expected expiration date of the Cure Period, and the process by which the General Partner intends to propose Successor Key Person(s) for approval by the limited partners.
Line 72: C&H will coordinate with Pinnacle Fund Services (Cayman) Ltd. (the \"Administrator\"), the Fund\'s third-party administrator, regarding the maintenance and accuracy of LP contact information, the appropriate method of delivery (including any notice provisions specified in the A&R LPA or in individual side letters), and the mechanics of distributing the Key Person Notice to all limited partners within the contractual timeframe. C&H will confirm with the Administrator that notice is delivered by a method that satisfies the delivery requirements of Section 15.01 of the A&R LPA.
Line 78: C&H will advise the Clients regarding the identification and evaluation of proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the development of a recommended successor governance framework for the Fund. This advisory work may encompass the following elements:
Line 80: > \(a\) **Designation of Successor Key Person(s).** C&H will advise on the criteria and process for designating one or more Successor Key Persons under the A&R LPA, including the qualifications, investment experience, and operational capabilities that limited partners are likely to consider in evaluating any proposed successor. C&H will assist in preparing biographical and professional materials for inclusion in the consent solicitation package.
Line 82: > \(b\) **Establishment of an Investment Committee.** In the event that the Clients determine that the successor governance framework should include the establishment of a formal Investment Committee or similar collective governance body (in lieu of, or in addition to, a sole Key Person designation), C&H will advise on the structure, composition, authority, and operating procedures of such body, and will prepare the necessary amendments to the A&R LPA to implement such structure.
Line 84: > \(c\) **Modifications to Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H will advise on potential modifications to the key-person provisions of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, which may include revised replacement periods, modified trigger events (including, for example, a threshold requiring the departure or incapacitation of more than one designated Key Person before a Key Person Event is deemed to occur), and other structural changes to reduce single-person dependency risk.
Line 86: > \(d\) **Carried Interest Reallocation.** C&H will advise the Clients on the legal and governance considerations associated with any proposed reallocation of carried interest among GP personnel in connection with the transition, including the interplay between the carried interest provisions of the A&R LPA and the operating agreement of DCM.
Line 92: **3.4 LPA Amendment Drafting**
Line 94: C&H will prepare one or more amendments to the A&R LPA (each, an \"LPA Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework developed pursuant to Section 3.3 above. It is anticipated that the LPA Amendments will include modifications to the following provisions of the A&R LPA, among others:
Line 102: > \(d\) Related schedules and exhibits, including the schedule of Key Persons attached to the A&R LPA.
Line 104: All LPA Amendments will be subject to the consent requirements set forth in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which generally requires the written consent of the General Partner and limited partners holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding GP co-investment) for amendments to certain specified provisions, including Section 8.04. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the applicable consent thresholds for each proposed amendment.
Line 108: C&H will advise on and coordinate the consent solicitation process necessary to obtain limited partner approval of the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. This workstream will include the following:
Line 110: > \(a\) **Successor Key Person Proposal Letter.** C&H will draft a detailed letter to all limited partners setting forth the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the rationale for the proposed designation(s), the terms of the proposed successor governance framework, and a summary of the proposed LPA Amendments (the \"Proposal Letter\"). The Proposal Letter will be designed to provide limited partners with all information reasonably necessary to make an informed decision regarding the proposed successor arrangements.

Line 114: > \(c\) **Coordination of Consent Solicitation Process.** C&H will coordinate the distribution of the Proposal Letter and Consent Form to all forty-seven (47) limited partners, working in conjunction with the Administrator to ensure accurate and timely delivery. Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), a Delaware limited liability company (EIN: 82-4917653), in its capacity as the General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. The Fund is governed by its Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated March 15, 2017 (as amended from time to time, the \"A&R LPA\"), which is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. The A&R LPA provides for certain key-person protections in favor of the Fund\'s limited partners, as more fully described in Section 3 below.

Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (holding a ninety percent (90%) membership interest) of DCM. This engagement letter confirms the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to the Clients (as defined below) in connection with the Key Person Event, including, without limitation, analysis of the A&R LPA\'s key-person provisions, preparation of required limited partner notifications, development of a successor governance framework, drafting of LPA amendments, and coordination of the limited partner consent solicitation process.

Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and sole designated \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA, suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024. The Proposal further introduces a series of governance enhancements, including the creation of a three-member Investment Committee.

The required approval threshold is consent of limited partners holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment. Based on voting LP commitments of \$2,798.25 million, the required consent threshold is \$1,865.50 million.

**IAC Role.** The proposed amendment would empower the IAC to designate one independent member to the newly created three-member Investment Committee, representing a material governance enhancement and a new fiduciary check on the General Partner\'s investment discretion. The five IAC members collectively hold \$1,140 million in voting LP capital commitments, representing approximately 40.7% of total voting LP commitments, and their collective support is therefore a critical --- though not independently sufficient --- factor in achieving the required 66⅔% consent threshold.

**Timeline Urgency.** As of the date of this memorandum, forty-nine days of the ninety-day Cure Period have elapsed, and forty-one days remain. The LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024 falls sixteen days before the Cure Period expiration on September 8, 2024. Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA provides, in relevant part:

The definition is name-specific, identifying Mr. Whitmore as the sole Key Person of the Fund. Notably, the provision does not include any other individual --- whether by name or by reference to a title, role, or position --- as a Key Person or co-Key Person. Nor does the definition include any provision for automatic succession or substitution in the event that Mr. Whitmore ceases to serve in such capacity. The designation is, in this respect, both narrow and rigid: it depends entirely on the continued active involvement of a single named individual.

Second, the absence of any automatic succession mechanism means that a Key Person Event cannot be cured by operation of the agreement itself. Rather, cure requires an affirmative act of LP consent to approve a Successor Key Person, as discussed in Section III.C.4 below. This structural feature gives the LP base significant leverage in the cure process, as the LPs effectively hold a veto right over the Fund\'s ability to continue active investment operations.

Third, we note that Section 8.04(a) does not define or cross-reference the concept of a \"Successor Key Person,\" which is addressed separately in Section 8.04(c). The two provisions operate in tandem but are structurally independent: Section 8.04(a) establishes who the Key Person is, while Section 8.04(c) establishes the mechanism by which a successor may be installed following a Key Person Event. There is no ambiguity in the current designation, and no basis for an argument that any other individual currently qualifies as a Key Person under the existing terms of the A&R LPA.

**1. Triggering Events Enumerated.** Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA provides that a \"Key Person Event\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the occurrence of any of the following events with respect to the Key Person:

Each of these triggering events is designed to address a different scenario in which the Key Person\'s active involvement in the Fund\'s operations is interrupted or terminated. Sub-clauses (i) through (iii) address definitive status changes (death, permanent disability, departure), while sub-clause (iv) addresses temporary or indefinite absences that may not rise to the level of the other triggers but nevertheless constitute a material disruption to the Fund\'s management.

The sub-clause (iv) trigger is particularly significant in this context because it operates on a short, seven-calendar-day timeline and does not require a determination of permanent disability or formal departure. It is, in effect, a \"business continuity\" trigger designed to ensure that LP interests are protected against even relatively short periods of Key Person absence that were not anticipated and disclosed in advance.

We note that the A&R LPA does not specify whether the seven-day period is measured inclusive or exclusive of the first day of inability. Under the convention most commonly applied in Delaware contract interpretation --- and consistent with the general rule that the day of the triggering event is excluded from the count --- the seven-day period would run from June 4 through June 10, yielding a trigger date of June 10, 2024. However, even under the alternative calculation (June 3 through June 9, yielding a trigger date of June 9, 2024), the Key Person Event has already occurred as of the date of this memorandum. For purposes of clarity and conservative calculation of downstream deadlines, we use June 10, 2024 as the operative trigger date throughout this memorandum.

**Permanent Disability.** The A&R LPA does not define \"permanent disability.\" In the absence of a contractual definition, a Delaware court would likely interpret the term in accordance with its ordinary meaning, informed by relevant context and, potentially, analogous definitions in related legal instruments (such as disability insurance policies, employment agreements, or the Americans with Disabilities Act). Under these authorities, \"permanent disability\" generally requires a showing that the individual suffers from a physical or mental condition that is expected to be of indefinite duration or to prevent the substantial performance of the individual\'s duties on a permanent or near-permanent basis.

The suspension takes effect as of the date of the Key Person Event --- June 10, 2024 --- and remains in effect until either (a) a Successor Key Person is approved by the requisite LP majority and the Investment Period is restored by operation of the cure mechanics, or (b) the Fund is wound down.

This prohibition encompasses both funded and unfunded commitments: the General Partner may not enter into new agreements, letters of intent, or other binding or non-binding arrangements to acquire new positions, nor may it draw on existing credit facilities for the purpose of funding new investments.

> • **Follow-On Investments Capped.** Follow-on investments --- defined as additions to existing portfolio positions held by the Fund as of the date of the Key Person Event --- are permitted, but are subject to an aggregate cap of \$28,700,000. An orderly liquidation of this portfolio --- particularly in the credit relative value book, which includes structured credit, distressed debt, and other less liquid instruments --- could require six to twelve (6--12) months, depending on prevailing market conditions and the willingness of counterparties to absorb the Fund\'s positions.

**Market Impact Costs.** The Fund\'s concentrated sector focus on asset management and banking amplifies the market impact risk of a forced liquidation. Selling a large, concentrated portfolio of financial sector equities and credit instruments into the market over a compressed timeframe would likely depress prices and generate adverse selection costs. The Fund\'s 1.85× gross leverage ratio further compounds this risk, as the Fund may need to reduce leverage rapidly by liquidating positions at unfavorable prices.

**Fire-Sale discounts on Illiquid Positions.** The credit relative value book is likely to include positions that cannot be liquidated quickly without accepting significant discounts to fair value. In a wind-down scenario, the Fund would be a known forced seller, which would further erode its negotiating position with potential purchasers.

**Carried Interest Crystallization.** A wind-down would trigger the accelerated crystallization of carried interest --- the economic impact of which (positive or negative) would depend on the relationship between liquidation values and the Fund\'s high-water mark. Given that the current NAV per unit of \$150.53 exceeds the high-water mark of \$142.67, the General Partner has accrued but uncrystallized carried interest that could be realized or lost depending on liquidation outcomes.

This memorandum has been prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP, in its capacity as fund counsel to Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\" or the \"General Partner\") and Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), at the request of DCM, to brief the Investor Advisory Committee (the \"IAC\") in advance of its meeting scheduled for July 29, 2024.
The purpose of this memorandum is to provide the IAC with a comprehensive summary of the following matters, each of which is expected to be discussed at the upcoming meeting:

> \(iv\) the IAC\'s specific role in the proposed successor governance framework, including the designation of an independent member to the newly created three-member Investment Committee, and the significance of the IAC members\' collective voting weight in the LP consent solicitation.

Calloway, Partner, and David Pineda, Senior Associate, has been provided with copies of all materials referenced herein, including the draft First Amendment, the Successor Key Person Proposal, and all supporting documentation. WCA is independently reviewing the proposed amendment on behalf of the IAC and is expected to provide its comments and recommendations to the IAC members separately. This memorandum is prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP in its capacity as fund counsel and does not purport to serve as independent legal advice to the IAC or any individual IAC member. (the \"DRULPA\"), the general partner of a Delaware limited partnership owes fiduciary duties to the limited partners, including the duty of loyalty and the duty of care, unless such duties are modified or eliminated by the partnership agreement. The General Partner has a fiduciary obligation to act in good faith in proposing Successor Key Persons and in the reallocation of carried interest. Whitmore is designated as \"Senior Advisor\" to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date. In such capacity, Mr. Whitmore shall have no governance authority, no voting rights with respect to any matter requiring the action or consent of the General Partner, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner. Mr. Whitmore\'s role as Senior Advisor shall be limited to providing non-binding advisory input on investment matters, to the extent his health permits, and shall be subject to the terms and conditions of a separate Senior Advisor Agreement between Mr. Whitmore and DCM.

The General Partner established August 23, 2024 as the deadline by which all Forms of Written Consent were required to be received by the General Partner (the \"LP Consent Deadline\"). The LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024 represents forty (40) calendar days from the July 15, 2024 circulation date of the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and the Form of Written Consent. The forty-day consent period was determined by the General Partner to be reasonable and consistent with the time periods customarily afforded to Limited Partners in similar circumstances, and was within the Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024. The General Partner also delivered reminder notices to all Limited Partners who had not yet returned executed Forms of Written Consent on August 5, 2024 and August 12, 2024, respectively.
**G. IAC Review.**

The Investor Advisory Committee (the \"IAC\") of the Partnership, established pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA, consists of five (5) members, each of whom is a representative of a Limited Partner of the Partnership. As of the date hereof, the members of the IAC are as follows:
> 1\. Diana Cortland, Representative of Northvale Public Employees\' Retirement System --- IAC Chair;

The IAC reviewed the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and related materials at a meeting held on July 29, 2024, at the offices of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, 51 West 52nd Street, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10019. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members (Ms. Cortland, Mr. Oshima, Ms. Mercer, Mr. Ashworth, and Ms. Al-Rashid) and by legal counsel to the IAC, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (Helen M. Calloway, Partner, and David Pineda, Senior Associate). Also in attendance at the invitation of the IAC were Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang, who presented their qualifications, investment philosophy, and proposed governance structure, and responded to questions from the IAC members and their legal counsel. The IAC meeting lasted approximately three hours and forty-five minutes. Following the presentation and discussion, the IAC unanimously confirmed that it did not object to the Successor Proposal or the First Amendment, and that the IAC would recommend to the Limited Partners that they approve the same. The IAC\'s recommendation was communicated to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners by separate letter from Ms. Cortland, as IAC Chair, dated August 1, 2024.

**1.1 Receipt of Written Consents.** The undersigned, on behalf of DCM as General Partner of the Partnership, hereby certifies that the General Partner has received duly executed Forms of Written Consent from thirty-eight (38) of the forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership (collectively, the \"Consenting LPs\"). Each Form of Written Consent received by the General Partner was executed by an authorized signatory of the respective Limited Partner and delivered to the General Partner in accordance with the delivery instructions set forth in the Form of Written Consent and the notice provisions of Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA. The General Partner has verified the authority of each signatory based on the relevant subscription documents, incumbency certificates, and/or powers of attorney on file with the Partnership.
**Section 2. Certification of Amendment Effectiveness.**

**2.1 Effectiveness of the First Amendment.** Having determined, as set forth in Section 1 above, that the requisite Limited Partner consent has been obtained in accordance with Sections 14.01 and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, and having further confirmed that all other conditions precedent to the effectiveness of the First Amendment have been satisfied (including, without limitation, the execution and delivery of the First Amendment by the General Partner on behalf of the Partnership), the General Partner hereby certifies that the First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. is effective as of August 26, 2024 (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"). The A&R LPA, as modified by the First Amendment, shall hereinafter be referred to as the \"LPA\" or the \"Partnership Agreement,\" and all references in any agreement, instrument, document, or certificate to the \"A&R LPA\" or the \"Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement\" shall be deemed to refer to the A&R LPA as amended by the First Amendment, unless the context otherwise requires.

**2.2 Summary of Key Amendments Now in Effect.** As of the Amendment Effective Date, the following material amendments to the A&R LPA, as effected by the First Amendment, are now in full force and effect:

> \(e\) *Designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor.* Marcus J. Whitmore is designated as Senior Advisor to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, with no governance authority, no voting rights, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner.

**2.3 Cure Period.** The 90-calendar-day Cure Period under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA commenced on the Key Person Event Date of June 10, 2024 and was set to expire on September 8, 2024. The effectiveness of the First Amendment on the Amendment Effective Date of August 26, 2024 --- which date is thirteen (13) calendar days prior to the expiration of the Cure Period --- constitutes a cure of the Key Person Event within the Cure Period, in accordance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA. Accordingly, the September 8, 2024 Cure Period expiration date is rendered moot.

Furthermore, the suspension of the Investment Period that took effect automatically upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event on June 10, 2024, pursuant to Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, is hereby terminated as of the Amendment Effective Date of August 26, 2024. The Investment Period shall continue from the Amendment Effective Date in accordance with its original terms as set forth in Section 7.01 of the A&R LPA (as amended by the First Amendment), and the General Partner (acting through the newly established Investment Committee) shall be permitted to make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Partnership, subject to the terms and conditions of the A&R LPA as amended by the First Amendment.
This Certificate may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which, taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned has executed this Certificate as of the date first written above.

This Exhibit A is an integral part of the Certificate of the General Partner Regarding Limited Partner Consent Tabulation and Effectiveness of the First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd., dated August 26, 2024. The information contained herein is confidential and is provided solely for the purposes described in the Certificate. The identities and capital commitments of the nine (9) non-consenting Limited Partners are not disclosed in this Exhibit A, in accordance with the confidentiality provisions of Section 16.03 of the A&R LPA.

This memorandum is an internal attorney work product of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, prepared for inclusion in the matter file. It is protected by the attorney-client privilege, the work product doctrine, and applicable rules of professional responsibility. This memorandum is not intended for distribution to any party outside of Calderwood & Harkness LLP without the prior written authorization of the Responsible Partner. Nothing herein constitutes a continuing obligation of the firm beyond the scope of the closed engagement.

All engagement objectives were achieved within the contractual Cure Period and in compliance with all applicable provisions of the A&R LPA, Delaware law, and Cayman Islands regulatory requirements. Thirty-eight (38) of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners delivered written consents representing \$2,412.8 million of LP capital commitments, or approximately 86.2% of voting LP commitments --- well in excess of the 66⅔% supermajority threshold required under Section 8.04(c). The First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on August 26, 2024, designating Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, establishing a three-member Investment Committee, transitioning Marcus J. Whitmore to a Senior Advisor role without governance authority, and implementing a revised carried interest allocation among the principals of DCM. The Cure Period deadline of September 8, 2024 was thereby mooted by the successful completion of the successor governance process thirteen (13) calendar days in advance.

The engagement is closed as of September 2, 2024. The matter status is: **closed_completed**. No outstanding legal issues, open work items, or continuing obligations of the Firm remain as of the date of this memorandum.

Graham Sutherland served as the Responsible Partner for the engagement and maintained oversight of all legal analysis, strategic recommendations, client communications, and substantive deliverables throughout the matter. Mr. Sutherland personally led the negotiation with Wexford Crane & Albright LLP on behalf of the Investor Advisory Committee and participated in the July 29, 2024 IAC meeting. Pamela Cross served as the Billing Partner and was responsible for all billing and engagement economics matters. Stephen Adler served as the Lead Associate and was principally responsible for the preparation of all memoranda, the drafting of the First Amendment, the LP consent solicitation process, and the tabulation of LP consents. Theresa Kim served as the Working Associate and supported all research, drafting, and document management functions throughout the engagement.

Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (\"WCA\") represented the interests of the Investor Advisory Committee throughout the review and negotiation period described in Section V.C below. WCA\'s representation was limited to the IAC and did not extend to any individual limited partner or to the limited partner body as a whole. The costs of WCA\'s representation were borne by the Fund in accordance with the IAC expense reimbursement provisions set forth in Section 9.04 of the A&R LPA.

**June 11, 2024 --- Engagement Opened.** Calderwood & Harkness LLP was formally engaged by DCM on June 11, 2024. The engagement letter was executed by Elaine R. Sato on behalf of DCM and by Graham Sutherland on behalf of C&H. Matter No. 1024-00002 was assigned. The engagement team was assembled immediately, and an initial conference call was held with Ms. Sato and DCM\'s General Counsel to receive a factual briefing on the circumstances of Whitmore\'s incapacitation and to discuss preliminary legal considerations.

**June 14, 2024 --- LP Notification Letter.** The LP Notification Letter was finalized, reviewed, and approved by C&H. The letter was signed by Elaine R. Sato in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer of DCM and distributed to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund via email (with contemporaneous hard copy via overnight courier). The notification disclosed the following: (i) the occurrence of the Key Person Event; (ii) the nature of the triggering circumstance (medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore); (iii) the automatic suspension of the Investment Period; (iv) the follow-on investment cap of \$28.7 million; (v) the commencement of the 90-day Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024; and (vi) DCM\'s intention to propose Successor Key Persons during the Cure Period. The LP Notification Letter was sent three (3) business days in advance of the contractual deadline of June 17, 2024, ensuring full compliance with the timing requirements of Section 8.04(c).

> \(b\) **Establishment of a Three-Member Investment Committee.** C&H recommended the creation of a formal Investment Committee under a new Section 8.05 of the A&R LPA. The Investment Committee was to be composed of three members: Sato (as Chair), Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee. The inclusion of an IAC-designated independent member was intended to enhance governance credibility and LP confidence, and to provide an institutional check on investment decision-making in the absence of Whitmore.

**Drafting of the First Amendment.** Based on the approved governance framework, C&H drafted the First Amendment to the A&R LPA, incorporating all of the recommended structural changes. C&H also prepared the Successor Key Person Proposal and Consent Solicitation Letter to the limited partners (the \"Successor Proposal Letter\"), which set forth the rationale for the proposed successor governance framework, summarized the key terms of the First Amendment, and enclosed the Form of LP Written Consent.

**July 15, 2024 --- Circulation to Limited Partners.** The Successor Proposal Letter, the draft First Amendment, and the Form of LP Written Consent were circulated to all forty-seven (47) limited partners on July 15, 2024. The consent solicitation established a deadline of August 23, 2024 --- forty (40) calendar days from the date of circulation --- for the return of executed LP consent forms.
**C. Phase 3: IAC Review and Negotiation (July 15--August 5, 2024)**

**IAC Briefing.** In advance of the IAC\'s review of the Successor Proposal and draft First Amendment, C&H prepared a comprehensive IAC Briefing Memorandum. The memorandum was distributed to the five members of the Investor Advisory Committee, who collectively represented \$1,140 million in capital commitments to the Fund. The IAC members, their affiliations, and their respective capital commitments were as follows:
**IAC Member**           **Affiliation**                                  **Role**                              **Capital Commitment**

The IAC Briefing Memorandum described the circumstances of the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences, the successor governance framework recommended by C&H and adopted by DCM, the key terms of the proposed First Amendment, and the consent solicitation process and timeline. The memorandum also included background information on the proposed Successor Key Persons, including their professional experience, roles at DCM, capital commitments to the Fund, and proposed carried interest allocations.

**July 29, 2024 --- IAC Meeting.** A formal meeting of the Investor Advisory Committee was held on July 29, 2024 by videoconference. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members and their respective representatives, as well as Graham Sutherland and Stephen Adler of C&H (on behalf of DCM) and Helen M. Calloway and David Pineda of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (as counsel to the IAC). Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang of DCM also participated in portions of the meeting to present their respective backgrounds, investment philosophies, and plans for the ongoing management of the Fund. The IAC meeting lasted approximately two and one-half hours and included a detailed discussion of the proposed governance framework, the qualifications of the Successor Key Persons, the scope of the independent Investment Committee member\'s authority, and the LP consent solicitation process.

**WCA Comments and Negotiation.** Following the IAC meeting, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, acting on behalf of the IAC, submitted written comments on the draft First Amendment. The principal areas of comment and negotiation included the following:

> \(i\) **180-Day Replacement Period Mechanics.** WCA sought clarification and additional specificity regarding the mechanics of the 180-day Replacement Period triggered by the loss of one Successor Key Person, including the process for identifying and proposing a replacement, the voting threshold applicable to the replacement, and the consequences of a failure to replace within the 180-day period. C&H responded with proposed language establishing a structured replacement process, including a requirement that the General Partner submit a replacement proposal to the IAC within sixty (60) days, followed by a full LP consent solicitation within the remaining period.

> \(ii\) **Scope of IAC-Designated Independent Investment Committee Member\'s Authority.** WCA advocated for enhanced authority for the IAC-designated independent member of the Investment Committee, including a veto right over investments exceeding a specified threshold. C&H, after consultation with DCM, agreed to grant the independent member a consultative role and a negative consent right on any single investment exceeding 5% of the Fund\'s NAV, but resisted the imposition of a general veto right, which C&H advised would be inconsistent with the General Partner\'s fiduciary obligations and the Fund\'s operational requirements.

**August 19, 2024 --- Consent Threshold Met.** As of August 19, 2024, the required LP consent threshold was met and exceeded. Thirty-eight (38) of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners delivered executed written consents to C&H, representing aggregate LP capital commitments of \$2,412.8 million. This amount constituted approximately 86.2% of the voting LP commitments of \$2,798.25 million, well in excess of the 66⅔% supermajority threshold of \$1,865.50 million required under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA. The consent threshold was achieved four (4) calendar days in advance of the August 23, 2024 deadline.

**August 26, 2024 --- First Amendment Effective.** The First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on August 26, 2024. The execution version was signed by DCM (by Elaine R. Sato as authorized signatory) and countersigned by the Fund. Copies of the executed First Amendment were delivered to all limited partners, the Investor Advisory Committee, the Fund\'s administrator, auditor, and prime broker, and the Cayman registered agent.

Following the effectiveness of the First Amendment on August 26, 2024, the C&H engagement team completed all remaining post-closing administrative matters, including the finalization and filing of all matter documents, the delivery of original and copies of executed documents to the appropriate parties, and the confirmation of notifications to Fund service providers. The Cure Period deadline of September 8, 2024 was mooted by the effectiveness of the First Amendment thirteen (13) calendar days in advance.

**September 2, 2024 --- Engagement Formally Closed.** The engagement was formally closed as of September 2, 2024. The matter status was updated to: **closed_completed**. No outstanding legal issues, open work items, or continuing obligations of the Firm remain as of the date of this memorandum.

> \(b\) **Loss of One Successor Key Person.** The loss of one Successor Key Person (whether by death, disability, resignation, termination, or other departure) triggers a 180-day Replacement Period. During the Replacement Period, the remaining Successor Key Person and the Investment Committee may continue to manage the Fund\'s investment activities without automatic suspension of the Investment Period. The General Partner must submit a replacement proposal to the IAC within sixty (60) days and conduct a full LP consent solicitation for the proposed replacement within the Replacement Period. If no replacement is approved within the 180-day period, the Investment Period is automatically suspended and standard cure mechanics apply.

> \(c\) **One independent member** --- to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA, as amended. The independent member shall have a consultative role and a negative consent right on any single investment exceeding 5% of the Fund\'s NAV, as negotiated with the IAC and its counsel.

> 2\. **Hard Copy Originals.** Original executed copies of the First Amendment to the A&R LPA and the GP Closing Certificate and Consent Tabulation shall be stored in the Firm\'s secure records vault (Vault Reference: NY-V-2024-0871). Access to vault materials is restricted to authorized personnel and requires Responsible Partner approval.

> 3\. **LP Consent Forms.** Copies of all executed LP consent forms received during the consent solicitation period shall be maintained in the matter file (both electronic and hard copy). Original executed consent forms have been delivered to DCM for its records.

> 4\. **Client Access.** DCM, as the client, is authorized to receive copies of all engagement deliverables upon request. Originals of the executed First Amendment have been delivered to DCM. Requests for additional copies or access to matter files should be directed to the Responsible Partner.

> 5\. **Cayman Registered Agent.** Archipelago Corporate Services Ltd., as the Fund\'s Cayman Islands registered agent, is to be furnished with copies of the executed First Amendment and such other documents as may be required for the Fund\'s statutory records and regulatory filings in the Cayman Islands. DCM has been advised to coordinate directly with Archipelago for this purpose.

> 6\. **Confidentiality.** All matter files remain subject to the attorney-client privilege, the work product doctrine, and the Firm\'s confidentiality obligations. No matter files shall be disclosed to any third party without the prior written consent of the client and the approval of the Responsible Partner, except as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order.

> 1\. **Ongoing GP Compliance.** The General Partner (DCM) is responsible for ongoing compliance with the provisions of the A&R LPA as amended by the First Amendment. This includes, without limitation, the designation of the IAC-nominated independent member of the Investment Committee pursuant to amended Section 9.02, the implementation and operation of the Investment Committee under new Section 8.05, and compliance with the revised key-person provisions of amended Section 8.04. These are ongoing obligations of DCM and do not require any further involvement of C&H absent a new engagement.

> 4\. **Future Key-Person Events.** Any future key-person event, successor designation, or further amendment to the A&R LPA would fall outside the scope of the closed engagement and would require a new engagement with C&H or other counsel selected by DCM.

All engagement objectives were achieved within the contractual 90-day Cure Period. The First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership became effective on August 26, 2024, thirteen (13) calendar days in advance of the Cure Period deadline of September 8, 2024. The LP consent solicitation was successfully completed, with consents received from 38 of 47 limited partners representing 86.2% of voting LP capital commitments, exceeding the required 66⅔% supermajority threshold. The successor governance framework, including the designation of Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, the establishment of the Investment Committee, the transition of Marcus J. Whitmore to Senior Advisor status, and the reallocation of carried interest entitlements, has been fully implemented.

Line 1826: A significant structural question in the CV transaction is whether the transfer of portfolio company shares from Fund II to the CV should be effected as a single-step or two-step process. Each approach has distinct tax consequences, and the optimal choice depends on balancing administrative efficiency against the need for clear QSBS tacking under Section 1202(h).
Line 1828: **Single-Step Approach: Fund II Contributes Directly to the CV.** Under this approach, Fund II would contribute the portfolio company shares directly to the CV in exchange for CV limited partnership interests, which would then be distributed to the Rolling LPs. This approach is administratively simpler --- it requires fewer intermediate transactions and documentation --- but raises questions regarding QSBS tacking. Specifically, Section 1202(h) addresses distributions of QSBS from a partnership to a partner (preserving QSBS status and tacking the holding period) but does not expressly address contributions of QSBS from one partnership to another partnership. There is limited direct authority on whether a partnership-to-partnership contribution preserves QSBS status.
Line 1830: Additionally, the single-step approach raises questions regarding the interaction with Fund II\'s existing Section 704(c) layers. Fund II may have its own Section 704(c) built-in gain allocations with respect to the portfolio company shares, and a direct contribution from Fund II to the CV would need to account for the tiering of these allocations through two partnership levels.
Line 1832: **Two-Step Approach: Fund II Distributes to Rolling LPs; Rolling LPs Contribute to CV.** Under this approach: (1) Fund II distributes the portfolio company shares in kind to the Rolling LPs, and (2) each Rolling LP contributes its share of the portfolio company stock to the CV in exchange for a CV limited partnership interest. This approach provides the clearest path to QSBS preservation because:

**(b) Section 721 Contribution Mechanics.** C&H will analyze and advise on the structuring of the contribution of Fund II\'s portfolio company interests to the CV as a tax-free contribution under Section 721 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"). Section 721 generally provides that no gain or loss is recognized to a partnership or any of its partners upon a contribution of property to the partnership in exchange for a partnership interest. Our analysis will address the application of Section 721 to the specific facts of the contribution, including whether the requirements for non-recognition treatment are satisfied and whether any exceptions to Section 721 (including contributions to investment companies under Section 721(b)) may apply.

We write on behalf of our client, Pinnacle Capital Management LLC (the \"Sponsor\"), in connection with the proposed formation of Pinnacle Continuation Vehicle LP (the \"Partnership\" or the \"CV\"). We have reviewed the draft Limited Partnership Agreement of the Partnership prepared by your office and dated July 28, 2025 (the \"Draft LPA\"), and we are providing herewith our markup limited to the tax-related provisions contained therein.

**Scope of Review.** Our review encompasses all Articles and Sections of the Draft LPA dealing with the following subject matters: (a) definitions of tax-related terms; (b) capital account maintenance and allocations of income, gain, loss, and deduction under Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"); (c) the distribution waterfall, including carried interest bifurcation and tax distribution mechanics; (d) tax elections, tax returns, and information reporting; (e) designation of the partnership representative under the centralized partnership audit regime enacted by the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015; (f) qualified small business stock (\"QSBS\") preservation covenants under Section 1202 of the Code; (g) Section 1061 carried interest compliance provisions; (h) withholding and indemnification provisions; (i) disguised sale protections under Section 707 of the Code; (j) Section 752 liability allocation provisions; and (k) blocker entity participation provisions for Tax-Exempt Partners and Non-U.S. Partners.

**Limitations.** Our review is limited to U.S. federal, state, and local tax provisions. Hawthorne Reid LLP retains primary responsibility for all non-tax provisions of the Draft LPA, including but not limited to governance, management authority, transfer restrictions, fiduciary duties, default remedies, exculpation and indemnification of the General Partner, and all other provisions not specifically addressed in this markup. We express no opinion on the non-tax provisions and have not reviewed them for this purpose.

> \(a\) **Comprehensive Rewrite of Section 704(c) Provisions.** The Draft LPA\'s Section 704(c) provisions are substantially incomplete and do not specify an allocation method. We have proposed a comprehensive rewrite specifying the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-3(d) for the \$1.202 billion of aggregate built-in gain in the Contributed Assets. The remedial method is the most equitable approach given the magnitude of the built-in gain and the negotiated expectation of the Secondary Investors (principally Garrison Secondaries Fund IV LP) that they will not bear pre-contribution tax gain. See the companion Section 704(c) Allocation Methodology Memorandum for a detailed comparative analysis of the traditional method, curative method, and remedial method.

> \(b\) **Addition of Legacy Carry Tranche / New Carry Tranche Bifurcation for Section 1061 Compliance.** The Draft LPA does not address Section 1061 of the Code or the three-year holding period requirement applicable to carried interest. We have added a new section bifurcating the General Partner\'s carried interest into a Legacy Carry Tranche (inheriting the Fund II holding period commencing December 2019, which has already satisfied the three-year requirement) and a New Carry Tranche (commencing on the Final Closing Date, with the three-year period not satisfied until October 31, 2028). This bifurcation is essential to preserve the favorable tax treatment of the legacy carry.

> \(c\) **Addition of QSBS Preservation Covenants.** The Draft LPA contains no QSBS-related provisions. Given that the three portfolio companies contributed to the Partnership are believed to qualify as QSBS under Section 1202 of the Code, and the potential Section 1202 exclusion represents a significant component of the value proposition for eligible Partners, we have added comprehensive QSBS preservation covenants.

> \(d\) **Addition of Mandatory Tax Distribution Provisions.** The Draft LPA does not include a mechanism for mandatory tax distributions. We have added a new section providing for quarterly tax distributions to each Partner based on such Partner\'s allocable share of estimated taxable income, multiplied by the highest combined marginal rate applicable to an individual residing in California (approximately 50.3%).

> \(e\) **Expanded Withholding and Indemnification Provisions.** The Draft LPA\'s withholding provisions are skeletal. We have expanded them to address Section 1446 (ECI withholding on Non-U.S. Partners), Section 1445 (FIRPTA withholding), state and local withholding obligations, and a comprehensive indemnification framework.

> \(f\) **BBA Partnership Audit Regime Provisions.** The Draft LPA\'s partnership representative provisions are outdated and reference the pre-BBA \"tax matters partner\" regime. We have proposed a complete rewrite to comply with the centralized audit regime under Sections 6221 through 6241 of the Code, including a commitment to the push-out election under Section 6226.

> \(g\) **blocker Entity Participation Provisions.** The Draft LPA makes passing reference to the use of blocker entities but does not include detailed provisions. We have added a new Article addressing the formation, capitalization, tax treatment, and governance of the Domestic blocker (PCV Domestic blocker Inc.) and the Offshore blocker (PCV International Holdings Ltd.).

\*\*\"Contributed Assets\"\*\* means the portfolio company interests contributed to the Partnership by Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership (EIN 84-3291067), at the Initial Closing, consisting of the following: (i) shares of common stock (and any preferred stock convertible into common stock) of Luminos Systems Inc., a Delaware corporation (EIN 47-8823156); (ii) shares of common stock (and any preferred stock convertible into common stock) of ClearArc Software Inc., a Delaware corporation (EIN 83-5519274); and (iii) shares of common stock (and any preferred stock convertible into common stock) of Vectral Cloud Inc., a Delaware corporation (EIN 85-1102847). The Contributed Assets are described in further detail in Schedule A hereto.

\*\*\"Legacy Carry Tranche\"\*\* means the portion of the Carried Interest attributable to the General Partner\'s pre-existing carried interest in Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (EIN 84-3291067), which is contributed (or \"rolled\") into the Partnership by means of a non-recognition transaction under Section 721 of the Code, and which inherits the original Section 1061 holding period commencing on or about December 2019 (the date of the final closing of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP). The three-year holding period applicable to the Legacy Carry Tranche under Section 1061(a) of the Code was satisfied as of December 2022. The Legacy Carry Tranche is further described in Section Z.2(a).

\*\*\"Rolling LP\"\*\* means any limited partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP that has elected to contribute its pro rata interest in the Contributed Assets to the Partnership in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Partnership, representing in the aggregate approximately \$680,000,000 in net asset value.

\*\*\"Secondary Investor\"\*\* means Garrison Secondaries Fund IV LP, a Delaware limited partnership, and any other investor acquiring a limited partnership interest in the Partnership in exchange for new cash capital contributions, and not by way of a contribution of interests in Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP.

This memorandum presents the recommended tax-optimal fund-level structure for Pinnacle Continuation Vehicle LP (\"PCV\" or the \"CV\"), a GP-led secondary continuation vehicle designed to hold three high-performing software and SaaS portfolio company stakes currently held by Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (\"Fund II\"). The proposed transaction is structured as a GP-led secondary / continuation vehicle transaction, a structure that has become increasingly prevalent in the venture capital and growth equity markets for extending the holding period of top-performing assets beyond the original fund term while providing liquidity options to existing limited partners.

**CV Capitalization.** The total capitalization of the CV at closing is expected to be approximately **\$1.074 billion**, comprised of: (a) approximately \$680 million in net asset value rolled into the CV by existing Fund II limited partners electing to continue their exposure to the portfolio (the \"Rolling LPs\"); (b) \$380 million of new capital committed by Garrison Secondaries Fund IV LP, the lead secondary buyer (Mitchell Adler, Partner; counsel: Whitfield & Calloway LLP, Douglas Whitfield, Partner); and (c) \$14 million of GP co-investment capital.
**Key Tax Objectives.** The tax structuring of the CV is designed to achieve the following principal objectives:

> \(a\) **Non-recognition treatment on contribution under Section 721.** The contribution of portfolio company shares from Fund II (or from Rolling LPs, as applicable) to the CV must qualify for non-recognition treatment under Section 721 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), thereby preserving the existing low tax basis and long-term holding periods in the contributed shares.

> \(c\) **Section 1061 holding period preservation for legacy GP carry.** The existing carried interest held by the GP in Fund II has satisfied the three-year holding period requirement under Section 1061 (applicable to \"applicable partnership interests\" or \"APIs\"). The CV structure must preserve this holding period through a rollover of the legacy carry into the CV, while appropriately delineating the new CV carry interest, which will commence a fresh three-year holding period.

> • The portfolio company shares will be contributed to the CV pursuant to **Section 721**, preserving basis, holding period, and QSBS status. The transfer will employ a **two-step distribution/contribution approach** (distribution from Fund II to Rolling LPs under Section 1202(h)(4)(A), followed by contribution from Rolling LPs to the CV under Section 721) to maximize QSBS tacking protection.

> • The GP carried interest will be **bifurcated into a legacy carry tranche** (rolling over the Fund II carried interest with its existing three-year holding period) and a **new carry tranche** (15% over 7% preferred return, with a fresh Section 1061 holding period commencing at closing).

Institutional investors, secondary buyers, and their respective counsel are familiar with the governance framework, fiduciary standards, and economic conventions of the Delaware limited partnership form. As discussed in Section IV.B below, the precise mechanics of the contribution --- whether Fund II contributes the shares directly to the CV in a single step or whether Fund II first distributes the shares to the Rolling LPs who then contribute them to the CV in a two-step process --- affect the analysis under both Section 721 and Section 1202. Under either approach, the contribution of property (portfolio company shares) in exchange for a partnership interest (CV limited partnership interest) falls squarely within the scope of Section 721(a), provided that the transaction is not recharacterized as a sale, exchange, or disguised sale under the rules discussed in Section IV.C below.

**Basis Consequences Under Section 722.** Under Section 722, the CV\'s basis in the contributed portfolio company shares will equal the contributing partners\' adjusted basis in those shares immediately before the contribution --- i.e., the carry-over basis from Fund II. The aggregate carry-over basis in the contributed shares is \$138 million (\$58.5M Luminos + \$37.4M ClearArc + \$42.1M Vectral). This means that the CV will hold shares with an aggregate FMV of \$1.34 billion and an aggregate tax basis of only \$138 million, necessitating the Section 704(c) allocation provisions discussed in Section VIII.

**Basis in CV Interests Under Section 723.** Under Section 723 (read in conjunction with the general basis rules applicable to partnership contributions), each Rolling LP\'s basis in its CV limited partnership interest will equal its adjusted basis in the portfolio company shares contributed (or, if the contribution is structured as a partnership-to-partnership transfer, its basis in its Fund II interest, as applicable). This ensures that the built-in gain is preserved at the partner level and will be recognized when the Rolling LP ultimately disposes of its CV interest or when the CV disposes of the contributed portfolio company shares.

**Holding Period Tacking Under Section 1223(1).** Under Section 1223(1), if property received in an exchange has the same basis (in whole or in part) as the property exchanged, the holding period of the received property includes the holding period of the exchanged property. Accordingly, the Rolling LPs\' holding period in their CV interests will include their holding period in the contributed portfolio company shares (or Fund II interests, as applicable), and the CV\'s holding period in the contributed shares will include the contributing partners\' holding period. This tacking is critical for maintaining long-term capital gain treatment and, as discussed in Section V, for preserving QSBS holding periods under Section 1202.

A significant structural question in the CV transaction is whether the transfer of portfolio company shares from Fund II to the CV should be effected as a single-step or two-step process. Each approach has distinct tax consequences, and the optimal choice depends on balancing administrative efficiency against the need for clear QSBS tacking under Section 1202(h).

**Single-Step Approach: Fund II Contributes Directly to the CV.** Under this approach, Fund II would contribute the portfolio company shares directly to the CV in exchange for CV limited partnership interests, which would then be distributed to the Rolling LPs. This approach is administratively simpler --- it requires fewer intermediate transactions and documentation --- but raises questions regarding QSBS tacking. Specifically, Section 1202(h) addresses distributions of QSBS from a partnership to a partner (preserving QSBS status and tacking the holding period) but does not expressly address contributions of QSBS from one partnership to another partnership. There is limited direct authority on whether a partnership-to-partnership contribution preserves QSBS status.

Additionally, the single-step approach raises questions regarding the interaction with Fund II\'s existing Section 704(c) layers. Fund II may have its own Section 704(c) built-in gain allocations with respect to the portfolio company shares, and a direct contribution from Fund II to the CV would need to account for the tiering of these allocations through two partnership levels.

**Two-Step Approach: Fund II Distributes to Rolling LPs; Rolling LPs Contribute to CV.** Under this approach: (1) Fund II distributes the portfolio company shares in kind to the Rolling LPs, and (2) each Rolling LP contributes its share of the portfolio company stock to the CV in exchange for a CV limited partnership interest. This approach provides the clearest path to QSBS preservation because:

> • **Step One** (distribution from Fund II to Rolling LPs) falls squarely within Section 1202(h)(4)(A), which provides that QSBS distributed by a partnership to a partner retains its QSBS character, and the partner tacks the partnership\'s holding period.

The two-step approach also avoids the complexities of tiered Section 704(c) layers, because Fund II\'s Section 704(c) obligations with respect to the portfolio company shares are resolved at the Fund II level upon distribution, and the CV establishes fresh Section 704(c) layers based on the difference between the shares\' FMV and carry-over basis at the time of contribution.

**Interaction with Fund II\'s Existing Section 704(c) Layers.** Fund II may have existing Section 704(c) layers with respect to the portfolio company shares if there were prior admissions of new limited partners at different valuations. Under the two-step approach, the in-kind distribution from Fund II to the Rolling LPs would trigger the application of Fund II\'s Section 704(c) allocations. We will need to coordinate with Andover & Strauss LLP to identify any existing Section 704(c) layers at the Fund II level and ensure that the distribution is properly accounted for.

> *Second*, the transaction is structured so that the cash to the cashing-out LPs flows through Fund II\'s existing distribution waterfall, not through the CV\'s distribution provisions. Garrison\'s capital is contributed to the CV, which then distributes cash to Fund II (or directly to the cashing-out LPs) to fund the liquidity elections. The Rolling LPs do not receive any distributions from the CV in connection with the closing.

> • **Debt-Financed Distribution Analysis**: If the CV incurs leverage at closing, distributions of borrowed funds could potentially trigger the disguised sale rules. However, the current transaction does not contemplate CV-level borrowing at closing; the cash for the cashing-out LPs is funded entirely by Garrison\'s equity commitment.

**Qualified Liability Exception Under Treas. Reg. § 1.707-5.** If the CV does assume or take property subject to any liabilities in connection with the contribution, the qualified liability exception under Treas. Reg. § 1.707-5 would need to be analyzed. As currently contemplated, the portfolio company shares are not subject to any liabilities, and the CV is not assuming any Fund II-level debt in connection with the transaction. Accordingly, this exception is not expected to be relevant.

**Allocation of CV-Level Debt Under Section 752.** Section 752 provides rules for the allocation of partnership liabilities among the partners, which can affect the disguised sale analysis (because an increase in a partner\'s share of partnership liabilities is treated as a contribution of money under Section 752(a), and a decrease is treated as a distribution of money under Section 752(b)). The current transaction does not contemplate CV-level borrowing at closing. If CV-level debt is subsequently incurred, the allocation of that debt among the partners will need to be analyzed for disguised sale implications.

> \(d\) The GP should avoid making any distributions from the CV to the Rolling LPs within two years of the closing (other than tax distributions, which are not treated as part of a disguised sale under Treas. Reg. § 1.707-4(a)(2)).
